paper_title: Another bijection for 021-avoiding ascent sequences
source_object: 021-avoiding ascent sequences: sequences $(u_1,\dots,u_n)$ of nonnegative integers with $u_1=0$ and $u_i \le 1 + \#\text{ascents in }(u_1,\dots,u_{i-1})$ for $i\ge 2$, and such that the nonzero entries are weakly increasing.
target_object: Dyck paths of semilength $n$: lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(2n,0)$ consisting of upsteps $U=(1,1)$ and downsteps $D=(1,-1)$ that never go below the $x$-axis.

algorithm_steps.description: Initialize the current Dyck path $P$ as the path $UD$ of size 1.

For $i=2$ to $n$, update $P$ according to $u_i$ using the following mutually exclusive cases. Let $a$ be the number of ascents in $(u_1,\dots,u_{i-1})$, $m$ its maximum entry, and $e$ the degree of elevation of $P$. In Case 4, $A_i = (m, m+1, \dots, a)$ if $u_{i-1}=0$, or $(m+1,\dots,a)$ if $u_{i-1}>0$; let $j$ be the position of $u_i$ in $A_i$, and $e\ge 0$ the degree of elevation of $P$.
After processing all entries, the final path $P$ is the image Dyck path.

inverse_steps.description: Start with the given Dyck path $P$ of size $n$, and set $i = n$.

While $P \neq UD$, determine $u_i$ and reduce $P$ according to the four cases. (1) If the last ascent of $P$ is long, set $u_i = 0$ and delete the last peak. (2) If the last ascent is short and $P$ is elevated, set $u_i = u_{i-1}$ and lower $P$ (remove first $U$ and last $D$). (3) If the last ascent is short and $P$ ends with $UD$, set $u_i = \text{valleys}(P)$ and delete the last peak. (4) Otherwise, mark the second downstep on the terminal descent; delete the last peak; locate the matching upstep of the marked downstep; transfer all upsteps before it in its ascent to the beginning of the path; set $u_i = \text{valleys}(P) - j$ where $j$ is the position of the marked downstep among key downsteps of the new path counted from right to left; then set $P$ to this new path. Decrease $i$ by $1$.
inverse_steps.math_formula:
$u_i \gets \begin{cases}
  0 & \text{if last ascent long},\\
  u_{i-1} & \text{if short and elevated},\\
  \operatorname{valleys}(P) & \text{if short and ends } UD,\\
  \operatorname{valleys}(P) - j & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}$
and $P$ updated correspondingly; $i \gets i-1$.

inverse_steps.description: When the loop ends ($P = UD$), set $u_1 = 0$. The sequence $(u_1,\dots,u_n)$ is the preimage.

paper_title: A bijection between triangulations and $312$-avoiding permutations
source_object: triangulations of an $n$-gon
target_object: the $312$-avoiding permutations of $\{1,2,\ldots, n-2\}$

algorithm_steps.description: Initialize empty sequence $\sigma$ and triangulation $T$ of an $n$-gon with vertices labeled $1,\ldots,n$.
While $|V(T)|>2$, find the vertex $v$ with the smallest label among those of degree 2. Append $v$ to $\sigma$ and delete $v$ and its incident edges from $T$.
Output the permutation $\sigma$.

inverse_steps.description: Given $\pi \in S_{n-2}(312)$. If $n=2$, return the degenerate triangulation (a single edge).

Set $k = \pi_{n-2}$ and write $\pi = A \, k \, B'$, where $A$ consists of the elements of $\{1,\ldots,k-1\}$ in the same relative order, and $B'$ consists of the elements greater than $k$; let $B$ be $B'$ with each entry reduced by $k$.
Recursively construct triangulations $T_A$ on vertices $\{1,\ldots,k-1,k,n\}$ (using $A$) and $T_B$ on vertices $\{k,k+1,\ldots,n-1,n\}$ (using $B$).
inverse_steps.math_formula: $T_A = \operatorname{clip}^{-1}(A)$ on polygon with vertices $1,\ldots,k-1,k,n$; $T_B = \operatorname{clip}^{-1}(B)$ on polygon with vertices $k,k+1,\ldots,n-1,n$.

inverse_steps.description: Merge $T_A$ and $T_B$ by identifying their common triangle $(k,n-1,n)$ to form a triangulation of the full $n$-gon.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $T = T_A \cup T_B$, where the triangle $(k,n-1,n)$ is shared.

paper_title: A bijection between triangulations and $312$-avoiding permutations
source_object: the decent $312$-avoiding permutations of $\{1,\ldots, n\}$ having up/down pattern $D^{i_1}U D^{i_2}U \cdots U D^{i_k}$
target_object: the dissections of an $(n-k+1)$-gon by $k$ diagonals

algorithm_steps.description: Apply the inverse of the clip-sequence bijection (Theorem 1) to obtain the triangulation $T$ of an $(n+2)$-gon whose clip sequence is $\pi$.
Write $\pi$ in descent blocks: $\pi = c_{11}\ldots c_{1i_1}\, c_{21}\ldots c_{2i_2}\, \ldots \, c_{k1}\ldots c_n$, where each block $c_{j1}>\ldots>c_{ji_j}$ and $c_{ji_j} < c_{(j+1)1}$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Decompose $\pi$ according to its up/down pattern.

algorithm_steps.description: In $T$, for each $j$, the triangles corresponding to ears $c_{j2},\ldots,c_{ji_j}$ form an $(i_j+2)$-gon. Remove the internal diagonals of these polygons, keeping only the boundary.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: For each $j$, let $P_j$ be the polygon formed by the ears $\{c_{j2},\ldots,c_{ji_j}\}$; remove all diagonals inside $P_j$.

algorithm_steps.description: The remaining triangles ($c_{j1}$) correspond to ears or boundary faces. Close the gaps by identifying adjacent vertices that become disconnected, resulting in a convex polygon dissection.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Merge vertices $v$ and $v+1$ if they are not connected after deletions, iterating through the circular order.

algorithm_steps.description: Relabel the vertices in circular order by $1,\ldots, n-k+1$ to obtain the final dissection.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Let $\phi$ be the order-preserving map from the remaining vertices to $[n-k+1]$.

inverse_steps.description: Given a dissection $D$ of an $(n-k+1)$-gon by $k$ diagonals, triangulate each face $F$ by adding diagonals from the second smallest vertex to all other non-adjacent vertices.
inverse_steps.math_formula: For each face $F$ with vertices $v_1<v_2<\ldots<v_m$, add diagonals $v_2v_j$ for $j=3,\ldots,m-2$.

inverse_steps.description: After triangulating, there are $k$ gaps corresponding to the original diagonals; insert a new vertex into each gap and relabel to obtain a triangulation $T$ of an $(n+2)$-gon.
inverse_steps.math_formula: Insert vertex $u_j$ between $v_{m_j-1}$ and $v_{m_j}$ for each face, and relabel sequentially.

inverse_steps.description: The clip sequence of the resulting triangulation is the desired decent 312-avoiding permutation.

paper_title: Type $D_n^{(1)}$ rigged configuration bijection
authors: Masato Okado, Reiho Sakamoto, Anne Schilling, Travis Scrimshaw
source_object: the set of highest weight elements in tensor products of Kirillov--Reshetikhin crystals $B = B^{r_k, s_k} \otimes \dots \otimes B^{r_2, s_2} \otimes B^{r_1, s_1}$ of type $D_n^{(1)}$
target_object: the set of unrestricted rigged configurations of type $D_n^{(1)}$

algorithm_steps.description: If $r_k \le n-2$, split off the leftmost column of the leftmost KR crystal using $\ls$. The bijection satisfies $\Phi(b) = \gamma( \Phi( \ls(b) ) )$.
If the leftmost KR crystal is a column ($s_k = 1$) and $r_k \le n-2$, split off the lowest box using $\lb$. Then $\Phi(b) = \beta( \Phi( \lb(b) ) )$.
If the leftmost KR crystal is a box ($r_k = s_k = 1$) and $r_k \le n-1$, delete the box using $\lh$. Then $\Phi(b) = \delta( \Phi( \lh(b) ) )$.
In the spin case ($r_k = n$ or $n-1$), use $\lh_s$ instead of $\lh$, and corresponding $\delta_s$. The bijection is defined recursively on the total number of boxes $\sum_i r_i s_i$.

Update the drawing: Redraw the matching using the new labels obtained from the first two reversals.

inverse_steps.description: Applying Procedure Triple Reverse again returns the original matching, since each reverse labelling is an involution.

source_object: Type OCOC set partition $\pi \in \mathfrak{P}_n$ on $[n]$, i.e., a set partition whose arc diagram (after possible inflation of transitory vertices) has the pattern of $n+k$ consecutive openers, $k$ closers, then possibly a transitory $v'$ (closer) and $v''$ (opener), then $j$ openers, and $n+j$ closers, all in one indecomposable interval.

algorithm_steps.description: Inflate any transitory vertex $v$: replace $v$ by two consecutive vertices $v'$ (closer) and $v''$ (opener) with $v'<v''$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $V' = (V \setminus \{v\}) \cup \{v', v''\}$, with $v'$ inheriting the closing incident arc and $v''$ the opening incident arc.

algorithm_steps.description: Reverse the labels of the first block of $(n+k)$ openers.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Let openers $O = \{o_1 < o_2 < \dots < o_{n+k}\}$. For vertex originally labeled $o_i$, new label $\tilde{o}_i = o_{n+k+1-i}$.

algorithm_steps.description: Reverse the labels of the last block of $(n+j)$ closers.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Let closers $C = \{c_1 < c_2 < \dots < c_{n+j}\}$. New label $\tilde{c}_i = c_{n+j+1-i}$.

algorithm_steps.description: Redraw the diagram with the new labels in increasing order and arcs connecting the same endpoints as before.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: For each arc $(x,y)$, draw arc $(\tilde{x}, \tilde{y})$ in the new ordering of vertices.

algorithm_steps.description: Reverse the labels of the closers (or openers) of the $n$ connecting arcs that go from the first indecomposable sub-block to the second.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Let these closers be $c'_1 < \dots < c'_n$. New label $\tilde{c}'_i = c'_{n+1-i}$.

algorithm_steps.description: Redraw the connecting arcs with the updated labels.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Adjust arcs $(x,y)$ to $(\tilde{x}, \tilde{y})$ for the connecting arcs.

algorithm_steps.description: Deflate $v'$ and $v''$ back to a single vertex $v$ (with original label), merging arcs.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Combine $v'$ and $v''$ into $v$: any arc ending at $v'$ now ends at $v$, any arc starting at $v''$ now starts at $v$. Renumber vertices $>v''$ by $-1$.

paper_title: A Bijection for Crossings and Nestings
source_object: Type OC permutation $\sigma \in \mathfrak{S}_n$ whose arc diagram (upper arcs) in each indecomposable interval consists of a block of consecutive openers followed by a block of consecutive closers (including a fixed point or upper transitory as an opener-closer pair). No lower transitories are present.
target_object: Permutation $\tau \in \mathfrak{S}_n$ with label $L(\tau)$ having the upper and lower nesting/crossing numbers swapped with the corresponding upper and lower crossing/nesting numbers.

algorithm_steps.description: Separate the permutation into an upper arc diagram $A_U$ (arcs with $a \le \sigma(a)$) and a lower arc diagram $A_L$ (arcs with $a > \sigma(a)$).
For each indecomposable interval in $A_U$, reverse the labels of all closers (right endpoints of upper arcs, including those from fixed points and upper transitories treated as opener-closer pairs).
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Let $C_U = \{c_1 < c_2 < \dots < c_m\}$ be the closers. New label $\tilde{c}_i = c_{m+1-i}$.

algorithm_steps.description: Redraw $A_U$ with the new labels in increasing order, drawing arcs between the same pairs as before, to obtain $A'_U$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: For each arc $(a,c) \in A_U$, draw arc $(\tilde{a}, \tilde{c})$ where $\tilde{a}$ is the new label of $a$ (if $a$ is an opener not in the reversed set, $\tilde{a}=a$).

algorithm_steps.description: For $A_L$, similarly reverse the labels of all closers (right endpoints of lower arcs, which are the smaller numbers).
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Let $C_L = \{d_1 < d_2 < \dots < d_k\}$ be the closers in $A_L$. New label $\tilde{d}_i = d_{k+1-i}$.

algorithm_steps.description: Redraw $A_L$ with the new labels to obtain $A'_L$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: For each arc $(a,d) \in A_L$, draw arc $(\tilde{a}, \tilde{d})$.

algorithm_steps.description: Combine $A'_U$ and $A'_L$ into a permutation $\tau$ by taking the union of the arcs as the new mapping.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\tau(x) = y$ for each arc $(x,y) \in A'_U \cup A'_L$.

paper_title: A note on a bijection for Schröder permutations
source_object: $\{4132, 4231\}$-avoiding permutations on $[0,n]$
target_object: Schr\"{o}der $n$-path: a lattice path from $(0,0)$ to $(n,n)$ with steps $N=(0,1)$, $D=(1,1)$, $E=(1,0)$ that never goes below the diagonal $y=x$

algorithm_steps.description: Compute the truncated coinversion table $c = (c_1,\dots,c_n)$ of the given permutation $p$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $c_i = \#\{j : 0 \le j < i, j \text{ precedes } i \text{ in } p\}$ for $i=1,\dots,n$.

algorithm_steps.description: Determine the set of fixed points $\operatorname{FP}(c)$ and the sorted multiset $L$ of non-fixed entries.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\operatorname{FP}(c) = \{i \in [n] : c_i = i\}, \quad L = c \setminus \operatorname{FP}(c) \text{ sorted increasingly}$.

algorithm_steps.description: Construct the Schr\"{o}der $n$-path step by step: start at $(0,0)$. For $x=0,1,\dots,n$ do: for each occurrence of $x$ in $L$, take an $N$ step; then if $x<n$, take a $D$ step if $x+1 \in \operatorname{FP}(c)$, otherwise take an $E$ step.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Initialize path as empty sequence. For $x = 0\dots n$: add $|L \cap \{x\}|$ copies of $N$; then if $x < n$, if $x+1 \in \operatorname{FP}(c)$ add $D$ else add $E$.

inverse_steps.description: From the Schr\"{o}der path $S$, record the $x$-coordinates of all $N$ steps in order to get multiset $L$, and record the set $F$ of $x$ where a $D$ step ends (i.e., the path has a $D$ step from $(x-1,x-1)$ to $(x,x)$).
inverse_steps.math_formula: $L = (x \text{ of each } N \text{ step in order}),\quad F = \{x \in [n] : S \text{ contains a } D \text{ step ending at } (x,x)\}$.

inverse_steps.description: Build the truncated coinversion table $c$: for $i=1,\dots,n$, if $i \in F$, set $c_i = i$; otherwise assign the remaining entries of $L$ to the positions $i \notin F$ in increasing order of $i$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: Let $L' = L$ (as multiset). For $i=1,\dots,n$: if $i \in F$ then $c_i = i$; else $c_i = \min(L')$, remove that element from $L'$.

inverse_steps.description: Reconstruct the permutation $p$ on $[0,n]$ from $c$: start with $p = [0]$; for $i=1,\dots,n$, insert $i$ into $p$ at position $c_i$ (0-indexed from the left).
inverse_steps.math_formula: $p \leftarrow [0]$; for $i=1,\dots,n$ do: insert $i$ into $p$ so that there are exactly $c_i$ elements smaller than $i$ to its left, i.e., at index $c_i$ in 0-based list.

algorithm_steps.description: 将$\lambda$写成$\lambda=\alpha^2\circ\beta$，其中$\alpha$的每个部分为奇数（来自$\lambda$中偶数重数的部分），$\beta$具有互不相同的奇数部分（来自$\lambda$中奇重数的部分）。记$t=\ell(\alpha)$。
对$\beta$应用Bressoud双射得到$\gamma^{(0)}\in\mathcal{S}(|\beta|)$。

依次对$i=1,\dots,t$，将$(2\alpha_i-1)^2$插入$\gamma^{(i-1)}$得到$\gamma^{(i)}$。插入算法：令$a=\alpha_i$。若$a=1$，则$\gamma^{(i)} = (\gamma^{(i-1)}_1+2,\gamma^{(i-1)}_2,\gamma^{(i-1)}_3,\dots)$；否则，构造组合$(2a,2a-2,\gamma^{(i-1)}_1,\gamma^{(i-1)}_2,\dots)$，并重复应用变换
$(2a-2j+2,2a-2j, \gamma^{(i-1)}_{2j-1},\gamma^{(i-1)}_{2j}) \mapsto (\gamma^{(i-1)}_{2j-1}+2,\gamma^{(i-1)}_{2j}+2, 2a-2j,2a-2j-2)$，
直至得到partition。最终形式由$j$和$a$决定，满足$\gamma^{(i)}_{2k-1}-\gamma^{(i)}_{2k}\in\{1,2\}$及相关的条件。
令$\mu = \gamma^{(t)}$，即为所求的distinct partition。

algorithm_steps.description: For a permutation $\sigma \in \SS$, set $\sigma_0=\sigma_{n+1}=0$. For $i=1,\dots,n$, determine the pattern at position $i$ (valley, peak, double rise, double fall) and assign $f(i)$: $f(i)=uu$ for valley, $f(i)=dd$ for peak, $f(i)=du$ for double rise, $f(i)=ud$ for double fall.
Form the word $P(\sigma) = \uparrow\, f(1)\, f(2)\, \dots\, f(n)\, \downarrow$.
Interpret $P(\sigma)$ as a Dyck word and obtain the corresponding Dyck shape $D_{n+1}$ of size $n+1$.
Remove the largest letter $n+1$ from $\sigma$ to obtain $\sigma'$. Recurse to define the profiles $P(\sigma^{(n)}),\dots,P(\sigma^{(0)})$ yielding Dyck shapes $D_n,\dots,D_1$.

inverse_steps.description: Given a chain $(D_0,\dots,D_n)$ (indexed from 0), assume having constructed $\tau$ for $(D_0,\dots,D_{n-1})$. Construct $\sigma$ such that $\sigma'=\tau$ and $P(\sigma)=D_n$.

Compare $D_{n-1}\,d\,d$ and $D_n$. If they differ at the $(2i)$th position, insert $n+1$ to the left of $i$ in $\tau$. If they differ at the $(1+2i)$th position, insert $n+1$ to the right of $i$ in $\tau$.

Backward shift: let $w$ be the left child of $v$ in $T'$. If the right subtree $B$ of $w$ is nonempty, let $v'_1,\dots,v'_\ell$ be all $\ominus$-nodes on the spine of $B$, and let $c_i$ be the number of $\oplus$-nodes on that spine between $v'_i$ and $v'_{i+1}$ (or below $v'_\ell$). inverse_steps.description: Forward shift: find $\oplus$-node $w$ immediately before the first $\ominus$-node by inorder, locate the first $\ominus$-node $v$ on the path from $w$ to root. Let $c_1$ be the number of $\oplus$-nodes between $v$ and $w$. Let $B$ be the right subtree of $w$. If $B$ nonempty, collect $\ominus$-nodes $v'_1,\dots,v'_\ell$ on its spine and counts $c_i$. Then apply $\mathcal{L}$ repeatedly.

Swing up: let $v_1$ be the topmost $\ominus$-node on the spine of $\tilde T^*$. Collect $\ominus$-nodes $v_1,\dots,v_{k-1},v_k=v$ on the path from $v_1$ to $v$. Then apply $\mathcal{L}^{-1}$ repeatedly.

algorithm_steps.description: Let $v_1$ be the first $\oplus$-node by inorder, $u_1$ its left child (or $\emptyset$). If $T_2=\emptyset$, set $T^*=(\emptyset,\ominus,\emptyset)$ and jump to Step 3.

algorithm_steps.description: If $T_2\neq\emptyset$, let $v_2$ be the lowest $\ominus$-node on the spine of $T_2$, $T_3$ its left subtree. Form $T^*$ as the conjugate of $((T\setminus T_1)\setminus T_3)/T_3(v,\emptyset)$.
Insert $T^*$: if $v_1=v$, set $\psi(T)=T_1/T^*(u_1,\emptyset)$; else set $\psi(T)=T_1/T^*(u_1, v_1)$.

inverse_steps.description: Locate the $(l+1)$-th initial $\ominus$-node $v$ and the $(l+2)$-th node $v_2$ (an $\oplus$-node). If $v_2$ not a descendant of $v$, set $\widetilde T = \overline{(\emptyset, v, \emptyset)}$ and jump to Step 3.

Otherwise, find the maximal left chain of $\ominus$-nodes starting at $v$, say $w_1=v,\dots,w_m$; extract $T^*$ with root $w_m$ and iroot $v$, let $T_1$ be the subtree with root $w_2$ (or $\emptyset$ if $m=1$). Set $\widetilde T = \overline{(T^*\setminus T_1)/T_1(\emptyset, v_2)}$.
If the root $w$ of $T$ coincides with $v$, set $\psi^{-1}(T) = (T\setminus T^*)/\widetilde T(u_1,\emptyset)$; else set $\psi^{-1}(T) = (T\setminus T^*)/\widetilde T(w,\emptyset)$.

algorithm_steps.description: Order the edges of $E$ as $e_1<e_2<\dots<e_n$. Orient $e_1$ arbitrarily.

\text{if } e_k\not\in T, & a=\min(C(T;e_k)),\; \text{orient } e_k \text{ opposite to } a \text{ in } C(T;e_k)

paper_title: A bijection between evil-avoiding and rectangular permutations
source_object: evil-avoiding permutations in \(S_n\); that is, permutations that avoid the patterns \(2413, 4132, 4213, 3214\)
target_object: rectangular permutations in \(S_n\); that is, permutations that avoid the patterns \(2413, 2431, 4213, 4231\)

algorithm_steps.description: Encode the rectangular permutation as a word in the regular language \(L_{\mathrm{rect}}\) by recursively determining the last operator applied using the first two entries (see Lemma 4.2).

Apply the bijection \(b : L_{\mathrm{rect}} \to L_{\mathrm{evil}}\) by substituting \(1\mapsto s\), \(2\mapsto p\), \(u\mapsto q\), \(d\mapsto r\) and reversing the prefix before the last \(r\) (if any).
algorithm_steps.math_formula: \(w' = \begin{cases} \text{reverse}(\text{sub}(w)_{\text{up to last } r}) \circ \text{sub}(w)_{\text{after last } r} & \text{if } r \in \text{sub}(w) \\ \text{sub}(w) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\) where \(\text{sub}(1)=s, \text{sub}(2)=p, \text{sub}(u)=q, \text{sub}(d)=r\)

algorithm_steps.description: Decode the resulting word \(w' \in L_{\mathrm{evil}}\) as an evil-avoiding permutation by interpreting its letters as operators \(\psi_p,\psi_q,\psi_r,\psi_s\) and applying them sequentially to the empty permutation \(e_0\).

Decode \(w \in L_{\mathrm{rect}}\) as a rectangular permutation by applying the operators \(\psi_1,\psi_2,\psi_u,\psi_d\) sequentially to \(e_0\).

paper_title: A bijection for partitions simultaneously $s$-regular and $t$-distinct
source_object: the set of partitions of $n$ simultaneously $s$-regular and $t$-distinct, i.e., partitions $\lambda \vdash n$ such that no part of $\lambda$ is divisible by $s$ and each part appears fewer than $t$ times
target_object: the set of partitions of $n$ simultaneously $t$-regular and $s$-distinct, i.e., partitions $\lambda \vdash n$ such that no part of $\lambda$ is divisible by $t$ and each part appears fewer than $s$ times

algorithm_steps.description: Factor $s$ and $t$ into primes: $s = (\prod_{i} p_i^{e_i}) (\prod_{j} q_j^{d_j})$, $t = (\prod_{i} p_i^{b_i}) (\prod_{k} v_k^{c_k})$, where the $q_j$ are primes appearing only in $s$, the $v_k$ only in $t$, and the $p_i$ are common. Set $s' = \prod_{j} q_j^{d_j}$.

Separate the parts of $\lambda$ not divisible by $s'$; call this subpartition $\lambda_1$. Apply the double Glaisher map $\phi_{s'} \phi_t$ to $\lambda_1$ to obtain a $t$-regular, $s'$-distinct partition $\lambda_1'$. Set aside this image.

Take the remaining parts (all divisible by $s'$) and divide each part by $s'$, obtaining a new partition $\lambda_{\text{rest}}$. (The factor $s'$ will be re-applied to frequencies after later steps.)
For each common prime $p_i$ (in a chosen order), perform the following substeps on the current $\lambda_{\text{rest}}$.
Extract from $\lambda_{\text{rest}}$ the subpartition $\rho$ consisting of parts not divisible by $p_i^{e_i}$.
For each part size $m$ in $\rho$, write its multiplicity in $\rho$ as $e(m) = a(m) + C(m) \cdot k$ with $0 \le a(m) < k$ and $0 \le C(m) < p_i^{b_i}$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $e(m) = a(m) + C(m) \cdot k$, $0 \le a < k$, $0 \le C < p_i^{b_i}$

algorithm_steps.description: Collect the $a(m)$ copies of each $m$ into a subpartition $\rho_a$ (which is $p_i^{e_i}$-regular and $k$-distinct) and apply $\phi_{p_i^{e_i}} \phi_k$ to obtain a $k$-regular, $p_i^{e_i}$-distinct partition $\rho_a'$.

For the $C(m)k$ copies of each $m$, form a partition where each such part $m$ is replaced by $C(m)$ copies of $m k$. Apply $\phi_{p_i}$ to obtain a partition $\rho_{Ck}'$ that is $p_i^{e_i}$-distinct and contains parts divisible by $k$ but not by $t$.

Combine $\rho_a'$ and $\rho_{Ck}'$ to form a $t$-regular, $p_i^{e_i}$-distinct partition. Multiply all frequencies by the cumulative factor $F$ (composed of $s'$ and previously wrapped prime powers). Add the result to the final output.
From $\lambda_{\text{rest}}$, remove the parts already processed (those not divisible by $p_i^{e_i}$) and divide the remaining parts by $p_i^{e_i}$ to continue the iteration.

Repeat step 4 for the next prime $p_{i+1}$, using the updated $\lambda_{\text{rest}}$ and accumulating the wrapping factor. After processing all common primes, the union of all previously set-aside subpartitions forms the image partition.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Final image = union of all $\rho'$ images (with appropriate frequency multipliers).

symbol_definitions.meaning: Glaisher's bijection: maps m-distinct partitions to m-regular partitions (and its natural extension to all partitions via part-frequency matrix transposition)

purpose_detail: 证明同时 $s$-regular 和 $t$-distinct 的分拆数与同时 $t$-regular 和 $s$-distinct 的分拆数相等

paper_title: Eulerian digraphs and Dyck words, a bijection
authors: Pietro Codara, Ottavio M. D'Antona, Marco Genuzio
source_object: the set $\mathscr{W}$ of Dyck words over the alphabet $\{x,D\}$ (words with equal numbers of $x$ and $D$, and no prefix has more $D$'s than $x$'s)
target_object: the set $\mathscr{M}_W$ of Dyck matrices, which are binary matrices satisfying conditions (M1) and (M2) in Definition 2.1, representing $\{s_1,\dots,s_n\}$-labelled Eulerian digraphs in $\mathscr{E}_W$ with an order on cycles

algorithm_steps.description: Initialize counters and output matrix $M$ as empty.

Read the input Dyck word character by character. When reading $D$, increment $\mathcal{D}$ and set $prev$ to $D$. When reading $x$, if the previous character was $x$, simply increment $X$; otherwise (a valley, i.e., $x$ after $D$), create a new row of the Dyck matrix, append it to $M$, fill previous rows with $0$'s, and reset counters.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: If $c = D$: $\mathcal{D} \gets \mathcal{D}+1$, $prev \gets ``D''$. If $c = x$ and $prev = x$: $X \gets X+1$. If $c = x$ and $prev = D$: let $R$ be a copy of the previous row (if any) keeping only the first $k$ ones and setting the rest to $0$; then append $(X-k)$ ones to $R$; set $M \gets [M; R]$ and for each previous row of $M$ append $(X-k)$ zeros; then $k \gets X-\mathcal{D}$, $X \gets k+1$, $\mathcal{D} \gets 0$, $prev \gets ``x''$.

algorithm_steps.description: After processing all characters, create the last row similarly and add it to $M$, filling previous rows with $0$'s.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Let $R$ be a copy of the previous row keeping only the first $k$ ones, then append $(X-k)$ ones; set $M \gets [M; R]$ and fill previous rows accordingly. Return $M$.

inverse_steps.description: Add a first and last row of all zeros to the input Dyck matrix $M$ to obtain $M'$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $M' \gets \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{0} \\ M \\ \mathbf{0} \end{bmatrix}$ where $\mathbf{0}$ is a row of $k$ zeros.

inverse_steps.description: Scan $M'$ column by column (or row by row using a $2\times1$ window) and build a word $w$ by appending $x$ for each $(0,1)$ pair and $D$ for each $(1,0)$ pair; skip $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: Initialize $w \gets \epsilon$. For $j=1$ to $k$, for $i=1$ to $n+1$: if $m'_{i-1,j}=0$ and $m'_{i,j}=1$, then $w \gets w \cdot x$; if $m'_{i-1,j}=1$ and $m'_{i,j}=0$, then $w \gets w \cdot D$. Return $w$.

paper_title: Foata's Bijection for Tree-Like Structures
source_object: the set $F(A,B,C,\gamma)$ of cycle-free functions, where $A,B,C$ are disjoint finite sets, $\gamma:B\to A$ is a surjection, and a function $f:A\to B\cup C$ is called cycle-free if for every $b\in B$ the sequence $(f\circ\gamma)^i(b)$ eventually terminates at some $c\in C$.
target_object: the set of functions $g:A\to B\cup C$ such that $g(a_1)\in C$ for some beforehand fixed $a_1\in A$.

algorithm_steps.description: Fix an ordering of $A$ and let $A=\{a_1,\dots,a_{|A|}\}$. Define $Z=(z_1,\dots,z_s)$ as the increasing sequence of elements in $A\setminus \gamma(f(A))$, assuming $\gamma(c)=c$ for $c\in C$.
Initialize an empty list of sequences.

For $i=1,\dots,s$: Let $m_i\ge0$ be the smallest integer such that $(\gamma\circ f)^{m_i+1}(z_i)$ either lies in $C$ or occurs in at least one of $\gamma\otimes\delta_1,\dots,\gamma\otimes\delta_{i-1}$, where $\gamma\otimes(x_1,\dots,x_t)=(\gamma(x_1),\dots,\gamma(x_t))$.
Construct the sequence $\delta_i$ as $\delta_i = \big( (f\circ\gamma)^{m_i}(f(z_i)), (f\circ\gamma)^{m_i-1}(f(z_i)), \dots, f(z_i) \big)$.

inverse_steps.description: From $g$ obtain the sequence $\delta$ (according to the fixed ordering of $A$). Recover $Z=A\setminus\gamma(g(A))$, sorted increasingly.
In $\gamma\otimes\delta$, identify $s$ positions where the entry either lies in $C$ or equals a previously occurring entry; these mark the beginnings of $\delta_1,\dots,\delta_s$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: Find indices $p_1<\dots<p_s$ such that for each $p_i$, the $p_i$-th element of $\gamma\otimes\delta$ is either in $C$ or equals $(\gamma\otimes\delta)_{p_j}$ for some $j<i$. Then $\delta_i$ are the corresponding segments of $\delta$.

inverse_steps.description: For each $i$, use $\delta_i$ and $z_i$ to recover $f$ via the relation $\delta_i = ((f\circ\gamma)^{m_i}(f(z_i)),\dots,f(z_i))$ and the definition of $m_i$ as $|\delta_i|-1$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: Set $m_i = |\delta_i|-1$. Then $f(z_i) =$ last element of $\delta_i$, and for $k=1,\dots,m_i$, $f(\gamma^k(f(z_i)))$ is determined iteratively from $\delta_i$ and $\gamma$.

symbol_definitions.meaning: the set of cycle-free functions as described
the increasing sequence of elements in $A\setminus\gamma(f(A))$
the sequence constructed for $z_i$
the operation $(x_1,\dots,x_t)\mapsto(\gamma(x_1),\dots,\gamma(x_t))$

purpose_detail: Prove that $|F(A,B,C,\gamma)| = |C|(|B|+|C|)^{|A|-1}$.

paper_title: Foata's Bijection for Tree-Like Structures
source_object: the set $Y$ of $H$-built-trees on $[n]$ rooted at $[m]$, where $H$ is a fixed $m$-graph on $[k]$, $l=e(H)$, $n=e(k-m)+m$, an $H$-built-tree consists of a $(k,m)$-tree $T$ with edges $E_1,\dots,E_e$ plus $H$-graphs $H_i$ on $E_i$ such that if $E_i\cap E_j$ is a lap (size $m$) then it is an edge of both $H_i$ and $H_j$; rooted at $[m]$ means $[m]\in\cup_i E(H_i)$.
target_object: $Z = F(A,B,C,\gamma) \times \prod_{i=1}^e \left( X_i \times \mathcal{R}_H \right)$, where $A=[e]$, $B=[e]\times[l-1]$, $C=\{[m]\}$, $\gamma:B\to A$ is the coordinate projection, $X_i = \left[\binom{(k-m)(e-i+1)-1}{k-m-1}\right]$, and $\mathcal{R}_H$ is the set of distinct $H$-graphs on $[k]$ rooted at $[m]$.

algorithm_steps.description: Order the edges of the $H$-built-tree $T$ as $E_1,\dots,E_e$ such that $[m]\in E(H_1)$ and each $E_i$ ($i\ge2$) shares a lap with some $E_j$, $j<i$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Choose an ordering $E_1,\dots,E_e$ satisfying the building condition.

algorithm_steps.description: Define $g'(E_1)=[m]$, and for $i\ge 2$, $g'(E_i)=E_i\cap\bigcup_{j=1}^{i-1}E_j$; define $f(E_i)=E_i\setminus g'(E_i)$ (the free part).
Relabel edges as $D_1,\dots,D_e$ so that $d_i = \min f(D_i)$ increases; let $H_i'$ be the $H$-graph on $D_i$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Renumber edges such that $d_1 < d_2 < \dots < d_e$ where $d_i = \min f(D_i)$.

algorithm_steps.description: Label all edges (laps) of $H_i'$ except $g'(D_i)$ by $(i,1),\dots,(i,l-1)$ in colex order; this yields indexing of edges by $A=[e]$ and laps by $B\cup C$ where $B=[e]\times[l-1]$, $C=\{[m]\}$. Define $g:A\to B\cup C$ by mapping $i$ to the label of $g'(D_i)$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $g(i) = \text{label of } g'(D_i)$; note $g(1)=[m]\in C$. The resulting $g$ is cycle-free.

algorithm_steps.description: For each $i=1,\dots,e$: index $(k-m-1)$-subsets of $\big(\bigcup_{j=i}^e f(D_j)\big)\setminus\{d_i\}$ in colex order by $X_i$, and let $x_i$ be the index of $f(D_i)\setminus\{d_i\}$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $x_i = \text{index of } f(D_i)\setminus\{d_i\} \text{ in the colex listing of } \binom{\bigcup_{j=i}^e f(D_j)\setminus\{d_i\}}{k-m-1}$.

algorithm_steps.description: Construct the bijection $h:D_i\to[k]$ that is monotone on $g'(D_i)$ and $f(D_i)$, mapping them onto $[m]$ and $[m+1,k]$; let $R_i\in\mathcal{R}_H$ be the image of $H_i'$ under $h$.
Output the tuple $(g, x_1, R_1, \dots, x_e, R_e) \in Z$.

inverse_steps.description: Input a code $(g, x_1, R_1, \dots, x_e, R_e)$. Determine $A=[e]$, $B=[e]\times[l-1]$, $C=\{[m]\}$.

Successively reconstruct $d_i$ and $f(D_i)$ for $i=1,\dots,e$: let $V = [n]\setminus\big(\bigcup_{j=1}^{i-1} f(D_j)\cup[m]\big)$, then $d_i = \min V$, and $f(D_i)\setminus\{d_i\}$ is the $x_i$-th $(k-m-1)$-subset of $V\setminus\{d_i\}$.

For $i$ with $g(i)\in C$: set $D_i = [m]\cup f(D_i)$, $g'(D_i)=[m]$, use $R_i$ and $h^{-1}$ to recover $H_i'$, thereby obtaining all other laps of $D_i$ (labelled $(i,1),\dots,(i,l-1)$). For $i$ with $g(i)\in B$ and already associated to a lap: reconstruct $D_i$ and $H_i'$ analogously.
inverse_steps.math_formula: If $g(i)\in C$: $D_i = [m]\cup f(D_i)$, $H_i' = h^{-1}(R_i)$ where $h$ is the standard bijection; extract laps $(i,1),\dots,(i,l-1)$.

symbol_definitions.meaning: set of $H$-built-trees on $[n]$ rooted at $[m]$
the target product set
set of distinct $H$-graphs on $[k]$ rooted at $[m]$
symbol_definitions.latex_def: $\mathcal{R}_H = \{ H\text{-graphs on }[k]\text{ containing }[m]\text{ as an edge} \}$

purpose_detail: Prove the enumeration formula for rooted $H$-built-trees, and as corollaries $(k,m)$-trees and $k$-gon trees.

paper_title: Foata's Bijection for Tree-Like Structures
source_object: edge-labelled trees (Cayley trees) with $n$ edges $e_1,\dots,e_n$, where $e_1=\{a,b\}$ is a distinguished edge, vertices are unlabelled, edges are labelled by $\{e_1,\dots,e_n\}$.
target_object: sequences $\delta$ of length $n-1$ with entries from $\{a,b,e_2,\dots,e_n\}$ that start with $a$.

algorithm_steps.description: Set $A = B = \{e_2,\dots,e_n\}$, $C = \{a,b\}$, $\gamma:B\to A$ the identity map.

For each edge $e\in A$, define $f(e)$: if $e$ shares a vertex with $e_1$, set $f(e)$ to that common vertex; otherwise let $f(e)$ be the first edge on the unique path from $e$ to $e_1$. This yields a cycle-free function $f\in F(A,B,C,\gamma)$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $f(e) = \begin{cases} x\in\{a,b\}\text{ if }e\cap e_1=\{x\} \\ e' \text{ where }e'\text{ is the neighbor of }e\text{ on the path to }e_1\end{cases}$.

algorithm_steps.description: Apply Foata's bijection to obtain the sequence $\delta$ (of length $|A|=n-1$) corresponding to $f$. By construction $\delta$ starts with an element of $C$; to ensure a bijection, we keep only those codes starting with $a$ (reversing $a,b$ otherwise).
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\delta = \text{Foata}(f)$, with $\delta_1 = a$ (after possibly swapping labels of $e_1$).

inverse_steps.description: Given a sequence $\delta$ starting with $a$, apply Foata's inverse to recover a cycle-free $f$ on $A,B,C,\gamma$ as above.

Reconstruct the edge-labelled tree: $e_1=\{a,b\}$. For each $e\in A$, if $f(e)\in C$ then $e$ is incident to $e_1$ at that vertex; if $f(e)\in B$ then $e$ is connected to the edge $f(e)$, continuing recursively.
inverse_steps.math_formula: Build the tree by attaching each $e$ according to $f(e)$.

symbol_definitions.meaning: the code sequence
the Cameron equivalence relation on edges
symbol_definitions.latex_def: smallest equivalence relation such that two edges are related if they intersect at a degree‑2 vertex

purpose_detail: Prove that the number of edge-labelled trees with $n$ edges is $(n+1)^{n-2}$, and describe the equivalence relation $\cong$ in terms of the code.

paper_title: A New Bijection Between Forests and Parking Functions
source_object: $F_n$, the set of all rooted forests on $n$ labeled vertices, drawn by the 3 rules (roots at top, trees from left to right by maximum label, siblings from left to right by maximum labels in their descendants).
target_object: $PF_n$, the set of all parking functions of length $n$, i.e., sequences $(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ such that its non-decreasing rearrangement $(b_1,\dots,b_n)$ satisfies $1\le b_i\le i$.

algorithm_steps.description: Convert the forest $F$ into a tree $T$ by adding a new vertex $n+1$ as the root and connecting it to each root of the trees in $F$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $T = F \cup \{ (n+1, r) \mid r \text{ is a root of a tree in } F \}$

algorithm_steps.description: Relabel the vertices of $T$ to obtain a decreasing tree $D$ and define the bijection $\theta_F$ from the old labels to the new labels. For each vertex $v$, find the maximum label $m$ among its descendants, assign $m$ to $v$, and rearrange the remaining labels of its descendants order-preservingly. This process is well-defined and independent of the order of vertices.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\theta_F(v) = \max \{ \text{old labels of } u \mid u \text{ is a descendant of } v \text{ in } T \}$; then recursively assign the remaining labels to the descendants preserving the relative order.

algorithm_steps.description: Construct the tree $I$ with the same underlying structure as $T$, where each vertex $v$ is labeled by $\inv(T:v)$, the number of inversions at $v$ in $T$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $I(v) = \inv(T:v) = |\{ (v,u) \mid v > u \text{ and } u \text{ is a descendant of } v \text{ in } T \}|$

algorithm_steps.description: Construct the tree $C$ with the same underlying structure as $T$, where each vertex is labeled by its post‑order index (from $1$ to $n+1$).

Form the tree $D\times (C-I)$ with two labels per vertex: plain labels from $D$ and circled labels from $C-I$. Write the circled labels in the order of the plain labels $1,2,\dots,n$ and drop the last circled label (which is always $\cirnum{1}$) to obtain the parking function $P$.

inverse_steps.description: From a parking function $P=(p_1,\dots,p_n)$, form $P'=(p_1,\dots,p_n,1)$. Apply the parking algorithm to $P'$ to obtain the actual parking sequence $Q=(q_1,\dots,q_{n+1})$. Let $\sigma$ be the permutation of cars $(1,\dots,n+1)$ in the order of the parking spaces (so $\sigma(i)$ is the car parked at spot $i$). Build three trees $D$, $I$, $C$ on the same vertex set $[n+1]$ with the same underlying structure: for each vertex, its parent is the nearest larger car to its right in $\sigma$. Label the vertices of $C$ with the parking space numbers $1,\dots,n+1$, $D$ with the car numbers $\sigma(1),\dots,\sigma(n+1)$, and $I$ with the jumps $\jump(P':c) = q_c - p_c$ (with $p_{n+1}=1$).
inverse_steps.math_formula: $P' = (p_1,\dots,p_n,1)$, $Q = PA(P')$, $\sigma = Q^{-1}$ (as a permutation of $[n+1]$). The tree structure: for each $c\in[n+1]$, the parent of $c$ is the nearest $c' > c$ that appears after $c$ in $\sigma$; $n+1$ is the root. $C(i) = i$ for $i\in[n+1]$, $D(i) = \sigma(i)$, $I(i) = q_{\sigma(i)} - p_{\sigma(i)}$.

inverse_steps.description: Reconstruct the tree $T$ from the decreasing tree $D$ and the inversion tree $I$ by reversing the relabeling of Step 2 of the forward map. For each vertex $v$, let $k = I(v)+1$. Among the labels of the descendants of $v$ in $D$, pick the $k$-th smallest label $m$, assign $m$ to $v$, and distribute the remaining labels to the descendants order-preservingly. This yields the original labeled tree $T$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: For each vertex $v$: let $S$ be the set of labels of the descendants of $v$ in $D$; let $m$ be the $(I(v)+1)$-th smallest element of $S$; set the new label of $v$ to $m$, then recursively assign $S\setminus\{m\}$ to the descendants preserving order.

inverse_steps.description: Remove the root $n+1$ from $T$ to obtain the forest $F$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $F = T \setminus \{ n+1 \}$ (remove the vertex and its incident edges)

symbol_definitions.latex_def: D \text{ is a tree on } [n+1] \text{ with } \theta_F(v) \text{ as label of vertex } v

purpose_detail: 构造非递归双射并证明森林的 inversion/leader/tree 统计量与停车函数的 jump/lucky/critical 统计量等分布, 从而双射地证明 Gessel-Seo 公式。

paper_title: A bijection between bargraphs and Dyck paths
source_object: Dyck paths $\DP$: lattice paths with steps $u=(1,1)$ and $d=(1,-1)$ that start at the origin, end on the $x$-axis, and stay weakly above the $x$-axis.
target_object: Bargraphs $\B$: lattice paths with steps $U=(0,1)$, $H=(1,0)$ and $D=(0,-1)$ that start at the origin and end on the $x$-axis, stay strictly above the $x$-axis except at the endpoints, and have no consecutive $UD$ or $DU$.

algorithm_steps.description: Compute the height sequence of the Dyck path $P$: the $y$-coordinate of the highest point of each step.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: \text{heights}(P) = (h_1, h_2, \dots, h_{2\sl(P)}), \quad h_i = \text{height of step } i

algorithm_steps.description: Partition the height sequence into maximal blocks of consecutive equal heights.
Transform each block $(H, c)$ into $\lfloor c/2 \rfloor$ columns of height $H$.
Concatenate all columns to obtain the height sequence of the bargraph.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: \bij(P) = \text{bargraph with column heights } H_1^{\lfloor c_1/2 \rfloor} H_2^{\lfloor c_2/2 \rfloor} \dots H_k^{\lfloor c_k/2 \rfloor}

inverse_steps.description: Write the bargraph as a sequence of column heights $h_1^{a_1} h_2^{a_2} \dots h_r^{a_r}$ with $a_i \ge 1$.
Insert zero-length blocks so that adjacent heights differ by $\pm 1$, $h_1 = h_r = 1$, and set $h_0 = h_{r+1} = 0$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: \text{augment sequence to } h_1^{a_1} h_2^{a_2} \dots \text{ with } |h_{i+1} - h_i| = 1, \; h_1 = h_r = 1

inverse_steps.description: Replace each $h_i^{a_i}$ according to the relative heights of neighboring blocks: if $h_{i-1} < h_i > h_{i+1}$ use $(ud)^{a_i}$; if $h_{i-1} < h_i < h_{i+1}$ use $(ud)^{a_i}u$; if $h_{i-1} > h_i > h_{i+1}$ use $(du)^{a_i}d$; if $h_{i-1} > h_i < h_{i+1}$ use $(du)^{a_i}$.
Concatenate all $u$ and $d$ steps to obtain the Dyck path.

paper_title: A simple and unusual bijection for Dyck paths and its consequences
source_object: $D\in\mathcal{D}_n$ (a Dyck path of semilength $n$)
target_object: $\bij(D)\in\mathcal{D}_n$

algorithm_steps.description: For each up-step in $D$, match it with the corresponding down-step that completes the tunnel.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $D = A\uparrow B\downarrow C$ where $A,B,C$ are Dyck paths and the matched $\uparrow$ and $\downarrow$ form a tunnel.

algorithm_steps.description: Define the permutation $\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_{2n}$ that gives the zigzag reading order.

Construct $\bij(D)$ step by step: for $i=1,\dots,2n$, let $k=\sigma_i$. If the step $D_k$ is the first step of its matched pair encountered in this order, append an up-step; otherwise append a down-step.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $$\bij(D)_i = \begin{cases} \uparrow & \text{if } \forall \ell < i,\; \{\sigma_\ell, M(\sigma_\ell)\} \neq \{\sigma_i, M(\sigma_i)\} \\ \downarrow & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$ where $M(j)$ is the index of the step matched to step $j$.

inverse_steps.description: From $D' = \bij(D)$, construct the word $W = w_1\cdots w_{2n}$ by setting $w_{\sigma_i} = \mathtt{o}$ if $D'_i$ is an up-step, and $w_{\sigma_i} = \mathtt{c}$ otherwise.

Match the $\mathtt{o}$'s and $\mathtt{c}$'s in $W$: label $\mathtt{o}$'s with $1,\dots,n$ in order of appearance under $\sigma$. When encountering a $\mathtt{c}$, match it with the unmatched $\mathtt{o}$ of largest label in the same half of $W$ (left half $i\le n$, right half $i>n$); if none, match with the unmatched $\mathtt{o}$ of smallest label in the opposite half.
inverse_steps.math_formula: For $i=1..2n$: if $w_{\sigma_i}=\mathtt{o}$, assign the smallest unused label; if $w_{\sigma_i}=\mathtt{c}$, find the unmatched $\mathtt{o}$ in the same half with largest label (if exists) else in opposite half with smallest label.

inverse_steps.description: Reconstruct $D$ by reading labels from left to right: the first occurrence of a label gives an up-step, the second gives a down-step.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $D_i = \begin{cases} \uparrow & \text{if label at position $i$ appears for the first time} \\ \downarrow & \text{if label at position $i$ appears for the second time} \end{cases}$

symbol_definitions.meaning: the main bijection on Dyck paths

paper_title: Bijections for refined restricted permutations
source_object: $\S_n(321)$ (the set of 321-avoiding permutations of $[n]$)
target_object: $\S_n(132)$ (the set of 132-avoiding permutations of $[n]$)

algorithm_steps.description: Apply the Robinson-Schensted-Knuth correspondence to $\sigma \in \S_n(321)$, yielding a pair of standard Young tableaux $(P,Q)$ of the same shape with at most two rows.

Construct a Dyck path $D = \knu(\sigma)$ from $(P,Q)$: for $i=1,\dots,n$, let $a_i = u$ if $i$ appears in the first row of $P$, and $a_i = d$ otherwise, forming word $A = a_1 \cdots a_n$. Let $B$ be the analogous word from $Q$. Then $D$ is the concatenation of $A$ and the reverse of $B$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $D = A \, \overline{B}^{\,R}$, where $A,B \in \{u,d\}^n$ and $\overline{B}^{\,R}$ is the reverse of $B$.

algorithm_steps.description: Map the Dyck path $D$ back to a 132-avoiding permutation $\tau = \krar^{-1}(D)$ via the diagram construction: place $D$ in an $n\times n$ grid, shade for each up-step the cells below and to the right in its column and for each down-step the cells above and to the left in its row (forming the Young diagram fitting in $(n-1,n-2,\dots,1)$). Then, for each row $i$ from $1$ to $n$, set $\tau(i)$ to be the column index of the leftmost shaded cell in that row, ensuring exactly one entry per column.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\tau(i) = \min\{ j \mid (i,j) \text{ is shaded in the diagram of } D,\; \text{and column } j \text{ not yet used} \}$

algorithm_steps.description: Label the vertices $v_1,\dots,v_n$ in breadth-first search order and let $\sigma$ be the associated permutation (the labels).
Construct the step sequence of the Motzkin walk: start at $0$, first step $+1$, then for $i=1$ to $n-1$, step $c(v_i)-1$ where $c(v_i)\in\{0,1,2\}$ is the number of children of $v_i$.
Let $\mathcal{N} = \{a_1<\dots<a_k\}$ be the indices of nodes (non-leaf vertices). By Lemma 3.2, each $a_i$ is the index of a right-to-left minimum of $\sigma$.

algorithm_steps.description: Decompose $\sigma$ into $\sigma^{(0)},\dots,\sigma^{(k)}$, where $\sigma^{(i)}$ is the renormalized permutation induced by $\sigma$ on indices $\{a_i+1,\dots,a_{i+1}\}$ ($a_0=0$, $a_{k+1}=n$).

Decorate the Motzkin walk: for each $i$ with $s_i \ge 2$, the step interval $[a_i+1,\, a_{i+1}-1]$ forms a descending sequence of length $s_i-1$; attach the permutation $\sigma^{(i)}$ to that descending sequence. (If $s_i=1$, the decoration is the trivial permutation $(1)$.)
algorithm_steps.math_formula: For $a_i+1\le j \le a_{i+1}-1$, the $j$-th step is $-1$; the sequence of steps from $a_i+1$ to $a_{i+1}-1$ receives the decoration $\sigma^{(i)}$.

algorithm_steps.description: Compute the ballot sequence $b_1 b_2 \dots b_n$ from the $321$-avoiding permutation $\pi = p_1 p_2 \dots p_n$.

Convert the ballot sequence into a lattice path $P$ from $(0,0)$ to $(n,n)$ by drawing a horizontal segment from $(i-1,b_i)$ to $(i,b_i)$ for $i=1,\dots,n$, and vertical segments to connect consecutive $b_i$ (plus a final vertical segment to $(n,n)$).
Rotate $P$ counterclockwise by $3\pi/4$ radians to obtain a Dyck path $D$ of semilength $n$.
Apply the inverse of the standard bijection $f$ (which maps $132$-avoiding permutations to Dyck paths) to $D$ to get the $132$-avoiding permutation $\pi'$.

algorithm_steps.description: Apply the map $\psi$ to obtain a Dyck path $D_1$. From the permutation matrix of $\pi$, draw a lattice path from the upper-left corner to the lower-right corner that leaves all crosses to the right and stays as close to the diagonal as possible; then convert each south step to $u$ and each east step to $d$.

Apply the inverse of the automorphism $\Psi$ on Dyck paths. $\Psi$ is defined by: match each up-step with its corresponding down-step; let $\sigma_i = (i+1)/2$ for odd $i$, $\sigma_i = 2n+1-i/2$ for even $i$; scan the input steps in order $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{2n}$; if the matching step of the scanned step has not been read yet, output $u$, else $d$. The inverse $\Psi^{-1}$ is computed similarly using the inverse permutation.

Apply $\varphi^{-1}$ where $\varphi$ is the standard bijection composed with a reflection. Reflect $D_2$ (reverse and swap $u/d$), then apply $f^{-1}$ (inverse of standard bijection) to obtain the $132$-avoiding permutation $\pi'$.

algorithm_steps.description: Compute the canonical reduced decomposition of the 321-avoiding permutation $\pi$: $\pi = (12\dots n)\sigma_1\dots\sigma_k$ where each $\sigma_i = s_{h_i}s_{h_i-1}\dots s_{t_i}$ with $h_i\ge t_i$ and $1\le h_1<\dots<h_k\le n-1$, satisfying $t_i\ge t_{i-1}+1$.

Build a Dyck path $P$ of semilength $n$ from the canonical reduced decomposition using the zigzag decomposition with $(x+y)$-labeling. For $\ell=k,k-1,\dots,1$, extract the zigzag strip (starting at the rightmost essential cell) whose label sequence $\{i,\dots,j\}$ yields $\sigma_\ell = s_j\dots s_i$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $P$ is the unique Dyck path whose zigzag decomposition gives $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_k$.

algorithm_steps.description: From the Dyck path $P$, obtain a $231$-avoiding permutation via the trapezoidal decomposition with $(x-y)$-labeling. Decompose recursively: $P$ splits into $Q_1 u Q_2 d$ where $u$ is the left arm of the rightmost essential cell touching the $x$-axis and $d$ is the last down-step; the current trapezoidal strip gives $\sigma'_k = s_j\dots s_i$; recursively process $Q_1,Q_2$ to get $\sigma'_1,\dots,\sigma'_{k-1}$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\pi' = (1\ 2\ \dots\ n)\,\sigma'_1\dots\sigma'_k$, where $\sigma'_i$ come from the trapezoidal decomposition of $P$.

algorithm_steps.description: Base case: empty permutation
Decomposable case: if $\pi = \sigma \oplus \tau$ (i.e., $\pi$ is the sum of two nonempty permutations), then reverse the order of the sum of their images.
Indecomposable case: if $\pi$ starts with $n$, write $\pi = \alpha(\sigma) = n \sigma$ with $\sigma \in \sym_{n-1}(231)$. Let $\tau = CK(\sigma) \in \sym_{n-1}(321)$.
Identify the left-to-right maxima in $\tau$ that are to the right of 1 and are not right-to-left minima. Let their indices be $a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_m$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $A = \{ i > \operatorname{pos}(1) \mid \tau_i \text{ is a left-to-right maximum and not a right-to-left minimum} \} = \{a_1, \dots, a_m\}$

algorithm_steps.description: Insert the new largest letter $n$ immediately to the left of 1. Form an intermediate permutation $\sigma$ of length $n$ by setting $\sigma_i = \tau_i$ for $i < r$, $\sigma_r = n$, and $\sigma_i = \tau_{i-1}$ for $i > r$, where $r = \operatorname{pos}(1)$ in $\tau$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\sigma_i = \begin{cases} \tau_i, & i < r \\ n, & i = r \\ \tau_{i-1}, & i > r \end{cases}$

algorithm_steps.description: Cyclically shift the values at the inserted position and the shifted positions of the left-to-right maxima. Overwrite $\sigma_r$ with $\tau_{a_m}$ (if $m\ge 1$, else leave as $n$), and for each $j=1,\dots,m$, set $\sigma_{a_j+1}$ to $n$ if $j=1$, otherwise to $\tau_{a_{j-1}}$. The resulting permutation is $CK(\pi)$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\sigma_r := \begin{cases} \tau_{a_m}, & m \ge 1 \\ n, & m=0 \end{cases}$; for $j=1,\dots,m$: $\sigma_{a_j+1} := \begin{cases} n, & j=1 \\ \tau_{a_{j-1}}, & j>1 \end{cases}$

paper_title: A bijection between ternary trees and a subclass of Motzkin paths
source_object: S-Motzkin path of length $3n$ with $n$ up steps ($U$), $n$ down steps ($D$), and $n$ horizontal steps ($H$) satisfying: (i) the first step is $H$; (ii) between every two $H$ steps there is exactly one $U$ step; (iii) the $k$-th $D$ step occurs after at least $k$ pairs of an $H$ and a $U$ step.
target_object: ternary tree with $n$ nodes, where each node has three ordered subtrees: left, middle, right.

algorithm_steps.description: Identify the last and penultimate returns to the $x$-axis. Let $r_1,\dots,r_m$ be the positions (step indices) where the path touches the $x$-axis. The last return is $r_m$, the penultimate is $r_{m-1}$. The subpath from $r_{m-1}$ to $r_m$ consists of an up step $U$, a path, and a down step $D$. Remove the leading $U$ and trailing $D$ to obtain $\mathcal{C}$.
Find the first horizontal step $H$ to the left of $\mathcal{C}$, i.e., the largest index $x < r_{m-1}$ such that $s_x = H$.

Find the farthest horizontal step $y$ to the left of $x$ such that the subpath from $y$ to $x$ (excluding $x$) is a Motzkin path (it never dips below the height of its start point and ends at the same height). Set $\mathcal{A}$ to this subpath.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $y = \min\{ j < x : s_j = H \text{ and } \operatorname{height}(s_{j+1}\cdots s_{x-1}) \geq 0,\ \operatorname{final\_height}=0 \},\ \mathcal{A} = s_{y+1} \cdots s_{x-1}$

algorithm_steps.description: The remaining steps form $\mathcal{B}$. It is the concatenation of the prefix up to $y$ and the subsequence between $x+1$ and the up step that introduces $\mathcal{C}$ (i.e., $r_{m-1}+1$).
Recursively apply $\Phi$ to $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$, $\mathcal{C}$ to construct the left, middle, and right subtrees, respectively. The empty path corresponds to an empty tree.

inverse_steps.description: Given the paths $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C}$ associated with the subtrees of a node. Locate the rightmost (last) up step $U$ in $\mathcal{B}$. Let $k$ be its index. Split $\mathcal{B}$ into $\mathcal{B}_1$ (from the start up to and including $k$) and $\mathcal{B}_2$ (the remainder).
Assemble the parent path by concatenating $\mathcal{B}_1$, $\mathcal{A}$, a horizontal step $H$, $\mathcal{B}_2$, an up step $U$, $\mathcal{C}$, and a down step $D$.
Repeat recursively for each node of the ternary tree, starting from the leaves and working upward to the root.
inverse_steps.math_formula: Apply the construction to every node, using its three subtree paths as $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C}$.

paper_title: A bijection for Delannoy paths
source_object: central Delannoy $n$-paths $\d_n$, lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,n)$ using steps $E=(1,0)$, $N=(0,1)$, $D=(1,1)$
target_object: Kimberling paths $\k_{n+1,n}$, lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n+1,n)$ where steps are restricted to have finite nonnegative slope (no vertical steps)

algorithm_steps.description: For a central Delannoy path $P\in\d_n$ with $k$ East steps (and hence $k$ North steps), label the $y$-coordinates of the terminal points of the East and North steps. Write the East-step heights in order as $y_1,\dots,y_k$ and the North-step heights as $x_1,\dots,x_k$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: For $i=1,\dots,k$, let $x_i$ be the $y$-coordinate of the $i$th North step, and $y_i$ the $y$-coordinate of the $i$th East step in $P$.

algorithm_steps.description: Form the interior vertices of the Kimberling path: $(x_i,y_i)$ for $i=1,\dots,k$.
Construct the Kimberling path by joining $(0,0)$, $(x_1,y_1)$, $(x_2,y_2)$, $\dots$, $(x_k,y_k)$, and $(n+1,n)$ in that order.

inverse_steps.description: Given a Kimberling path $Q\in\k_{n+1,n}$ with interior vertices $V_1,\dots,V_k$, let $A$ be the set of $x$-coordinates of the interior vertices, and $B$ be the multiset of $y$-coordinates.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $A = \{x_i : (x_i, y_i) \text{ interior vertex}\}$, $B = \{y_i : (x_i, y_i) \text{ interior vertex}\}$.

inverse_steps.description: Define $C = \{1,2,\dots,n\} \setminus A$.
Arrange the elements of $A$ and $B$ (each labeled by its origin set) in weakly increasing order, with an $A$ element placed before a $B$ element of the same value. This gives a sequence $L$.
Insert each element of $C$ into $L$ as far left as possible while maintaining a weakly increasing sequence. This yields a sequence $S$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $S = \text{leftmost insertion of } C \text{ into } L \text{ preserving weak increase}$.

inverse_steps.description: Interpret $S$ as a sequence of steps: replace elements from $A$ by $N$, $B$ by $E$, and $C$ by $D$. This yields the central Delannoy path $\phi^{-1}(Q)$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $\phi^{-1}(Q) = \text{path corresponding to } S \text{ with } A\mapsto N, B\mapsto E, C\mapsto D$.

paper_title: A Natural Bijection between Permutations and a Family of Descending Plane Partitions
source_object: descending plane partitions of order $n$ with $k$ rows and no special part, denoted $a=(a_{i,j})$ where $1\le i\le k$, $i\le j\le \mu_i+i-1$, satisfying: $\mu_1\ge\cdots\ge\mu_k$, $a_{i,j}\ge a_{i,j+1}$, $a_{i,j}>a_{i+1,j}$, $a_{i,i}>\mu_i-i+1$, $a_{i,i}\le\mu_{i-1}-i+2$, and no special part (i.e., $a_{i,j}>j-i$ for all $i,j$).
target_object: permutations of size $n$ with exactly $k$ ascents, written as a concatenation of $k+1$ decreasing sequences $\beta^{(1)}\beta^{(2)}\cdots\beta^{(k+1)}$.

algorithm_steps.description: Initialize the permutation to the completely decreasing permutation of $\{1,\dots,n\}$.

For each row $i=1$ to $k$ (the DPP has rows $\alpha^{(1)},\dots,\alpha^{(k)}$): let $m_i$ be the length of row $i$, and let $S$ be the set of numbers in the last decreasing block of the current permutation (initially the whole permutation). Apply the order-preserving bijection $\phi:S\to\{1,\dots,|S|\}$.

From the $i$th row $\alpha^{(i)} = (a_{i,i}, a_{i,i+1}, \dots, a_{i,i+m_i-1})$, construct the strictly decreasing sequence $\gamma_{\text{raw}} = (a_{i,i}, a_{i,i+1}-1, \dots, a_{i,i+m_i-1} - (m_i-1))$ of positive integers $\le m_{i-1}$.
Map $\gamma_{\text{raw}}$ back to $S$ using $\phi^{-1}$ to obtain the new decreasing block $\gamma^{(i+1)}$ of length $m_i$; let $\gamma^{(i)}$ be the remaining elements of $S$ in decreasing order.
Replace the last decreasing block of the current permutation by the concatenation $\gamma^{(i)} \gamma^{(i+1)}$, thus creating an additional ascent.

inverse_steps.description: Starting from the right end of the permutation with $k$ ascents, let the last decreasing block be $\gamma^{(k+1)}$ of length $m_k$, and let the preceding block up to the previous ascent be $\gamma^{(k)}$; set $S = \gamma^{(k)} \cup \gamma^{(k+1)}$ with $|S| = m_{k-1}$.
Let $\psi: S \to \{1,\dots,m_{k-1}\}$ be the order-preserving bijection. Compute the image $\psi(\gamma^{(k+1)})$, a strictly decreasing sequence.
Recover the $k$th row of the DPP: $a_{k,k+j-1} = \gamma'_j + (j-1)$ for $1\le j\le m_k$.
Remove the processed blocks, leaving a permutation with $k-1$ ascents, and repeat until all rows are recovered.

algorithm_steps.description: Let $E=\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}$ with $e_1=p$. Let $B$ be a uniactive internal basis. Choose the orientation of $p$ arbitrarily (this determines which of the two opposite bounded reorientations is obtained).

paper_title: The Active Bijection 2.b - Decomposition of activities for oriented matroids, and general definitions of the active bijection
source_object: the set of activity classes of reorientations of an ordered oriented matroid $M$
target_object: the set of bases of $M$

algorithm_steps.description: Given a basis $B$, compute its active partition (a mapping $\ass$ from $E$ to $\Int(B)\cup\Ext(B)$) and the corresponding active filtration by a single pass over $E$ in increasing order. For each $e$: if $e\in\Int(B)$, $e$ is internal and $\ass(e)=e$; if $e\in B\setminus\Int(B)$ and there is an external $c<e$ in $C^*(B;e)$, $e$ is external and $\ass(e)=\ass(c)$ (choose $c$ with greatest $\ass(c)$); otherwise $e$ is internal and $\ass(e)=\ass(c)$ with smallest $\ass(c)$; dual rules for $e\notin B$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\ass(e_k) = \begin{cases} e_k & \text{if } e_k\in\Int(B)\\ \ass(c) \text{ with } c = \arg\max_{c<e_k,\ c\text{ external in }C^*(B;e_k)} \ass(c) & \text{if } e_k\in B\setminus\Int(B) \text{ and such } c \text{ exists}\\ \ass(c) \text{ with } c = \arg\min_{c<e_k,\ c\text{ internal in }C^*(B;e_k)} \ass(c) & \text{if } e_k\in B\setminus\Int(B) \text{ and no such } c \text{ exists} \end{cases}$ and similarly for $e_k\notin B$.

algorithm_steps.description: For each $e_k$, determine its reorientation: if $e_k$ is internally or externally active, set its reorientation arbitrarily (this yields the $2^{\io+\ep}$ elements of the activity class).

For $e_k\in B\setminus\Int(B)$, let $a$ be the smallest element in $C^*(B;e_k)$ with $\ass(a)=\ass(e_k)$. Reorient $e_k$ if needed so that $e_k$ and $a$ have opposite signs in $C^*(B;e_k)$. For $e_k\notin B$ but not externally active, let $a$ be the smallest element in $C(B;e_k)$ with $\ass(a)=\ass(e_k)$ and reorient analogously.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\operatorname{sgn}_{C}(e_k) = - \operatorname{sgn}_{C}(a)$ with $C = C^*(B;e_k)$ if $e_k\in B$, else $C = C(B;e_k)$.

source_object: The set of dual-bounded reorientations of an ordered oriented matroid $M$ with respect to $p=\min(E)$, with fixed orientation for $p$ (i.e., $p\notin A$ for $-_AM$)
target_object: The set of uniactive external bases of the underlying matroid of $M$ (bases with internal activity 0 and external activity 1)

algorithm_steps.description: Given a uniactive external basis $B$, construct the unique dual-bounded reorientation with fixed orientation for $p$ by processing elements in increasing order.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Start with $e_1=p$ not reoriented. For $k=2$ to $n$: if $e_k\in B$, let $a=\min(C^*(B;e_k))$, reorient $e_k$ if necessary so that $a$ and $e_k$ have opposite signs in $C^*(B;e_k)$; if $e_k\notin B$, let $a=\min(C(B;e_k))$, reorient $e_k$ if necessary so that $a$ and $e_k$ have opposite signs in $C(B;e_k)$.

inverse_steps.description: For a given dual-bounded reorientation $-_AM$, apply duality: $\alpha(-_AM)=E\setminus\alpha((-_{A\triangle\{p\}}M)^*)$ (or equivalently, use the sign criterion of Definition \ref{def:cyc-alpha1}) to obtain the basis.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $\alpha(-_AM)=E\setminus\alpha((-_{A\triangle\{p\}}M)^*)$ or the basis $B$ satisfying: for all $b\in B$, the signs of $b$ and $\min(C^*(B;b))$ are opposite in $C^*(B;b)$; for all $e\in (E\setminus B)\setminus\{p\}$, the signs of $e$ and $\min(C(B;e))$ are opposite in $C(B;e)$.

purpose_detail: Proof of $t_{0,1}=o_{0,1}/2$: number of uniactive external bases equals half the number of dual-bounded reorientations with fixed orientation for $p$.

algorithm_steps.math_formula: $P = C_1 C_2 \cdots C_k$, where each $C_i$ is a primitive Grand Schröder path from $(x_{i-1},0)$ to $(x_i,0)$ not meeting GL in between, and each $C_i$ lies either entirely above $y=0$ or entirely below $y=0$.

algorithm_steps.description: For each component $C$, apply the mapping $\phi$ defined below, then concatenate the images to obtain $\Phi(P) \in \b_n$.
[Below component] If $C$ lies entirely below GL, reflect it vertically across GL: exchange $U \leftrightarrow D$, keep $F$ unchanged.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $C' = \text{reflect}(C)$, where $\text{reflect}: U \mapsto D,\; D \mapsto U,\; F \mapsto F$.

algorithm_steps.description: [Below component] Replace every peak $UD$ by a flatstep $F$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\phi(C) = \text{flatten}(C')$, where $\text{flatten}$ replaces each occurrence of $UD$ with $F$.

algorithm_steps.description: [Above component] Delete the first step (necessarily $U$) and the last step (necessarily $D$). Let $P_1$ be the resulting path.
[Above component] Replace every flatstep $F$ by a downstep $D$ immediately followed by an upstep $U$. Mark the new vertices that lie on GL (the endpoints of these $D$'s) as highlighted ($H$).
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $P_2 = \sigma(P_1)$, where $\sigma: F \mapsto D\,U$. Let $H$ be the set of vertices on $y=0$ that are created by the inserted $D$ steps.

algorithm_steps.description: [Above component] Flip (vertical reflection) the initial segment from the origin $O$ to the first highlighted vertex, and also every component that starts at a highlighted vertex (i.e., maximal subpaths from a point in $H$ to the next return to GL).
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $P_3 = \text{flip}_{H}(P_2)$, where $\text{flip}_{H}$ reflects across GL the subpath from $O$ to the first vertex of $H$, and every subpath that starts at a vertex of $H$ and ends at GL.

algorithm_steps.description: [Above component] Identify $V_1$, the leftmost among the lowest vertices of $P_3$, and $V_2$, the last vertex on GL that is the endpoint of an upstep $U$.
[Above component] Interchange the two segments $O$ to $V_1$ and $V_1$ to $V_2$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Write $P_3 = A \cdot B \cdot C$, where $A$ is the part from $O$ to $V_1$, $B$ from $V_1$ to $V_2$, and $C$ the remainder. Then $P_4 = B \cdot A \cdot C$.

algorithm_steps.description: [Above component] Flatten all peaks ($UD \to F$) except the one that now occurs at $V_2$ (i.e., if $V_2$ is followed by a $D$, keep that $UD$ intact).
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $P_5 = \text{flatten\_except}(P_4, V_2)$, which replaces every $UD$ pair by $F$ unless the vertex $V_2$ is the midpoint.

algorithm_steps.description: [Above component] Prepend an upstep $U$ and append a downstep $D$ to restore the original length.
[Above component] The resulting path $P_6$ is a Schröder component with exactly one peak. Set $\phi(C) = P_6$.

inverse_steps.description: Decompose $Q \in \b_n$ at GL into indecomposable components $D_1,\dots,D_k$.

For each component $D$, apply the inverse of $\phi$: if $D$ has no peak, expand every $F$ to $UD$ then reflect vertically; if $D$ has one peak, reverse the above‑component steps (remove first/last $U/D$, expand $F$ to $UD$ except at the peak, unswap the segments, flip back, replace $DU$ by $F$, prepend/append $U/D$).
inverse_steps.math_formula: $\psi(D) = \begin{cases} \text{reflect}(\text{unflatten}(D)) & \text{if $D$ has no peak}, \\ \text{inverse\_above\_steps}(D) & \text{if $D$ has exactly one peak}. \end{cases}$

inverse_steps.description: Concatenate the recovered components to obtain the preimage in $\a_n$.

paper_title: New bijective proofs pertaining to alternating sign matrices
source_object: $\text{GMT}(\mathbf{k})$ for any $\mathbf{k} \in \mathbb{Z}^n$
target_object: $\text{SGT}(\mathbf{k})$

algorithm_steps.description:
Base case $n=1$: $	ext{GMT}(\mathbf{k})=	ext{AR}_1$, $	ext{SGT}(\mathbf{k})=	ext{GT}(\mathbf{k})=(\{k_1\},\emptyset)$. Map $
warrow \mapsto k_1$, and pair $
earrow \leftrightarrow 
xarrow$.

For $n>1$, parse input as $T = (\mu^{(n)}, \mathbf{k}^{(n-1)}, \mu^{(n-1)}, \ldots, \mathbf{k}^{(1)}, \mu^{(1)})$. Let $\mu = \mu^{(n)}$, $\mathbf{l} = \mathbf{k}^{(n-1)}$, and $T'$ be the remainder, a $\text{GMT}(\mathbf{l})$.
Recursively apply $\Gamma_{\mathbf{l}}$ to $T'$ to obtain $U = (A, T_A) \in \text{SGT}(\mathbf{l})$, i.e., $A \in \text{GT}(T_A(\mathbf{l}))$, $T_A \in \text{AP}_{n-1}$.

Apply $\Phi_1$: use the sijection $\rho_{\mathbf{k}, x}$ (with $x = +\infty$) to transform the $\text{GT}$-part. This yields a new parameter $\mathbf{m} \in S_1 \times \cdots \times S_{n-1}$ and a $\text{GT}$ pattern $B$ with bottom row $(m_1+c_1(T_A),\ldots,m_{n-1}+c_{n-1}(T_A), x)$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\Phi_1(\mu, A, T_A) = (\mu, T_A, \mathbf{m}, B)$ where $B \in \text{GT}(m_1+c_1(T_A),\ldots,m_{n-1}+c_{n-1}(T_A), x)$

algorithm_steps.description: Apply $\Phi_3'$: a sijection that reorganises the $\mathbf{m}$ parameters and inserts $x$ into the bottom row at some position $i$, producing a $\text{GT}$ pattern of the form $\text{GT}(m_1(\mu,T_A,0),\ldots,m_{i-1}(\mu,T_A,0), x, m_i(\mu,T_A,1),\ldots)$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\Phi_3'(\mu, T_A, \mathbf{m}, B) \in \bigsqcup_{i=1}^n \text{GT}(m_1(\mu,T_A,0),\ldots, m_{i-1}(\mu,T_A,0), x, m_i(\mu,T_A,1),\ldots, m_{n-1}(\mu,T_A,1))$

algorithm_steps.description: Apply $\Phi_4'$: using the bijection $\Psi_{n,i}$ that maps $(\mu, T_A) \in \text{AR}_n \times \text{AP}_{n-1}$ to $T' \in \text{AP}_n$ (combining arrows), then apply $\tau$ to eliminate $x$ and obtain an element of $\text{SGT}(\mathbf{k})$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\Phi_4'(\mu, T_A, i, \ldots) = \tau(\text{GT}(k_1+c_1(T'),\ldots,k_{i-1}+c_{i-1}(T'), x, k_{i+1}+c_{i+1}(T'),\ldots, k_n+c_n(T'))) = (T', B') \in \text{SGT}(\mathbf{k})$

paper_title: New bijective proofs pertaining to alternating sign matrices
source_object: $\text{GMT}(\mathbf{k})$ for any $\mathbf{k} \in \mathbb{Z}^n$
target_object: $\text{AR}_n \times \text{SGT}(\mathbf{k})$

algorithm_steps.description: Base case $n=1$: $\text{GMT}(\mathbf{k})=\text{AR}_1$, $\text{AR}_1 \times \text{SGT}(\mathbf{k}) = \text{AR}_1 \times (\{k_1\},\emptyset)$. The identity sijection works.
For $n>1$, decompose $T = (\mu^{(n)}, \mathbf{k}^{(n-1)}, \dots) \in \text{GMT}(\mathbf{k})$ as $\mu = \mu^{(n)}$, $\mathbf{l} = \mathbf{k}^{(n-1)}$, and $T' \in \text{GMT}(\mathbf{l})$.

Recursively apply the sijection to $T'$ to obtain an element of $\text{AR}_{n-1} \times \text{SGT}(\mathbf{l})$, i.e., a pair $(\nu, (A, T_A))$ with $\nu \in \text{AR}_{n-1}$, $A \in \text{GT}(T_A(\mathbf{l}))$, $T_A \in \text{AP}_{n-1}$.
Reassociate: $(\mu, (\nu, (A, T_A))) \equiv (\nu, (\mu, (A, T_A)))$. This yields an element of $\text{AR}_{n-1} \times \bigsqcup_{\mu, \mathbf{l}} \text{SGT}(\mathbf{l})$.
Apply $\text{id} \times \Phi_1$ to the $\text{SGT}$ part: as in the previous bijection, transform $(A, T_A)$ using $\rho_{\mathbf{k}, x}$ to get $(\mathbf{m}, B)$ with $B$ having an extra row $x$.
Apply $\text{id} \times \Phi_3'$ to move $x$: obtain an index $i$ and a $\text{GT}$ pattern with $x$ inserted at position $i$.

Apply $\Phi_4''$: combine $\mu$ and $T_A$ into a new arrow pattern $T' \in \text{AP}_n$ using the bijection $\text{AR}_n \times \text{AP}_{n-1} \to \text{AR}_1 \times \text{AP}_n$, then apply $\tau$ to remove $x$, yielding an element of $\text{AR}_1 \times \text{SGT}(\mathbf{k})$. Finally, merge the $\text{AR}_{n-1}$ factor with the resulting $\text{AR}_1$ to get an element of $\text{AR}_n \times \text{SGT}(\mathbf{k})$.

source_object: \Fdown{n} = \{\text{transposition sequences } \mathbf{s} = (s_1, \dots, s_{n-1}) \mid s_i \in \sym_n \text{ transpositions, } \product(\mathbf{s}) = (n, n-1, \dots, 1)\}
target_object: \VT_n = \{\text{trees on } n \text{ vertices, each vertex receives a distinct label from } [n]\}

algorithm_steps.description: Compute the dual transposition sequence using the algebraic formula.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\mathbf{t} = \dual(\mathbf{s}) = \bigl( s_1,\; s_2^{s_1},\; s_3^{s_2 s_1},\; \dots,\; s_{n-1}^{s_{n-2} \cdots s_1} \bigr)$, where $\sigma^{\tau} = \tau^{-1} \sigma \tau$.

algorithm_steps.description: Interpret $\mathbf{t} \in \Fup{n}$ as a labeled tree: vertices $[n]$, and for each $i = 1,\dots,n-1$, if $t_i = (a,b)$, add an edge between $a$ and $b$ with label $i$.

Relabel vertices to obtain a tree in $\VT_n$: keep vertex $1$ with label $1$. For each other vertex $v$, let $e_v$ be the edge incident to $v$ that lies on the unique path from $v$ to $1$ (the edge closest to $1$). Let $w$ be the label of $e_v$. Assign to $v$ the new label $1+w$. Finally, erase all edge labels.

inverse_steps.description: Given $T \in \VT_n$, for each vertex $v \neq 1$ with label $\ell(v)$, let $e_v$ be the edge incident to $v$ closest to vertex $1$. Label $e_v$ with $\ell(v)-1$. Remove all vertex labels except $1$.

Recover the vertex labeling of the transposition sequence in $\Fup{n}$ by following the minimal increasing greedy trails starting from vertex $1$. Define $\wk_1$ using the edge-labeled tree: start at $1$, always take the smallest label larger than the previous edge. The order in which vertices are first visited yields labels $1,2,\dots,n$. This gives a transposition sequence $\mathbf{t} \in \Fup{n}$ where $t_i = (a,b)$ if the $i$-th edge traversed connects $a$ and $b$ (edges are processed in increasing label order).
inverse_steps.math_formula: $t_i = (a,b)$ where $\{a,b\}_i$ is the $i$‑th edge in the order of edge labels.

inverse_steps.description: Apply the dual again to recover $\mathbf{s} \in \Fdown{n}$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $\mathbf{s} = \dual(\mathbf{t}) = \bigl( t_1,\; t_2^{t_1},\; t_3^{t_2 t_1},\; \dots,\; t_{n-1}^{t_{n-2} \cdots t_1} \bigr)$.

paper_title: A simple bijection between permutation tableaux and permutations
source_object: $\{\sigma \in \mathfrak{S}_n : \operatorname{des}(\sigma)=k\}$, where $\operatorname{des}(\sigma) = \{i \in [n] : \text{if } \sigma(j)=i \text{ then } \sigma(j)>\sigma(j+1)\}$
target_object: $\{T \in \operatorname{PT}(n) : \operatorname{col}(T)=k\}$, where $\operatorname{PT}(n)$ is the set of permutation tableaux of length $n$ (Ferrers diagram filled with 0/1 such that each column has at least one 1, and no 0 has a 1 above it and a 1 to its left in the same row)

algorithm_steps.description: Construct the Ferrers shape and label rows and columns from the descents of $\sigma$. For $i=1,\dots,n$, step $i$ is West if $i$ is a descent, South otherwise. Rows are labeled by South steps (non-descents), columns by West steps (descents).
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $R = \{i : i \notin \operatorname{Des}(\sigma)\}$, $C = \operatorname{Des}(\sigma)$, and for each $i \in R$, $\lambda_i = |\{j \in C : j > i\}|$.

algorithm_steps.description: Initialize an empty tableau $T$ of shape $\lambda$, and set the current permutation $\sigma_{\text{cur}} = \sigma$.

While $T$ has empty cells, let $(i,j)$ be the eastmost-southmost empty cell (lexicographically maximal $(i,j)$ with $T(i,j)=\emptyset$). If $i$ and $j$ are not adjacent in $\sigma_{\text{cur}}$ (i.e., $|\operatorname{pos}_{\sigma_{\text{cur}}}(i)-\operatorname{pos}_{\sigma_{\text{cur}}}(j)| \neq 1$), set $T(i,j)=1$. Otherwise, if $i$ precedes $j$, set all empty cells in row $i$ to $0$ and delete $i$ from $\sigma_{\text{cur}}$. If $j$ precedes $i$, set $T(i,j)=1$, all empty cells in column $j$ to $0$, and delete $j$ from $\sigma_{\text{cur}}$. Repeat until all cells are filled.
algorithm_steps.math_formula:
While $\exists (i,j)\in\lambda$ with $T(i,j)=\emptyset$:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(i,j) &= \max\{(i',j') : T(i',j')=\emptyset\} \quad \text{(lexicographic by row then column)}\\
\text{if } &|\operatorname{pos}_{\sigma_{\text{cur}}}(i)-\operatorname{pos}_{\sigma_{\text{cur}}}(j)| \neq 1, \text{ then } T(i,j)=1;\\
\text{else if } &\operatorname{pos}_{\sigma_{\text{cur}}}(i) < \operatorname{pos}_{\sigma_{\text{cur}}}(j), \text{ then } \forall j'\text{ with } T(i,j')=\emptyset,\, T(i,j')=0,\; \sigma_{\text{cur}} \leftarrow \sigma_{\text{cur}}\setminus\{i\};\\
\text{else } &(\operatorname{pos}_{\sigma_{\text{cur}}}(j) < \operatorname{pos}_{\sigma_{\text{cur}}}(i)),\text{ then } T(i,j)=1,\; \forall i'\text{ with } T(i',j)=\emptyset,\, T(i',j)=0,\; \sigma_{\text{cur}} \leftarrow \sigma_{\text{cur}}\setminus\{j\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

algorithm_steps.description: The remaining $\sigma_{\text{cur}}$ is the increasing list of labels of the unrestricted rows (rows with no restricted zero) of $T$.

inverse_steps.description: Initialize $\sigma$ as the increasing list of labels of the unrestricted rows of $T$ (rows with no restricted zero, i.e., no $0$ that has a $1$ above it in the same column).
inverse_steps.math_formula: $R_{\text{unrest}} = \{ i \in R : \not\exists j \text{ with } T(i,j)=0 \text{ and } \exists i'<i,\, T(i',j)=1\}$, $\sigma = \text{sort}(R_{\text{unrest}})$.

inverse_steps.description: For each column $j$ from left to right: let $i = \min\{ r : T(r,j)=1\}$ (topmost 1). Insert $j$ immediately before $i$ in $\sigma$. If column $j$ contains rightmost restricted zeros (restricted zeros with no restricted zero to their right in the same row) in rows $i_1 < i_2 < \dots < i_k$, then for $r = k$ down to $1$, insert $i_r$ immediately before $j$ in $\sigma$.
inverse_steps.math_formula:
For each column $j$ in left-to-right order:
\[
\begin{aligned}
i &= \min\{ r : T(r,j)=1 \},\\
\sigma &\leftarrow \text{insert } j \text{ right before } i \text{ in } \sigma;\\
\text{let } I &= \{i_1<\dots<i_k\} \text{ be rows with rightmost restricted zero in column } j;\\
\text{for } r &= k \text{ down to } 1,\ \sigma \leftarrow \text{insert } i_r \text{ right before } j.
\end{aligned}
\]

inverse_steps.description: After processing all columns, the resulting $\sigma$ is the pre-image permutation.

algorithm_steps.description: Find the smallest element $i$ in the first block $B_1$ such that $\pi$ splits as $\pi = \pi_{[i-1]} \circ (\pi_{[i,n]} - i + 1)$.
Let $j$ be the smallest element in the underlying set of $R(\pi_{[i,n]})$; then $R(\pi_{[i,n]}) = \pi_{[j,n]}$.
Define $\varphi(\pi) = \pi_{[j-1]} \,|\, (\pi_{[j,n]} - j + 1)$, the slash product of the restriction before $j$ and the shifted restriction from $j$.

inverse_steps.description: For $\sigma\in\US_n\setminus\A_n$, let $j = \min(\operatorname{underlying}(R(\sigma)))$ and let $B_r$ be the first block of $R(\sigma)$.
If $\sigma_{[j-1]}$ is unsplitable, set $\psi(\sigma) = \sigma_{[j-1]} \circ (\sigma_{[j,n]} - j + 1)$.

Otherwise, find the smallest $i\in B_1$ such that $\sigma_{[j-1]} = \sigma_{[i-1]} \circ (\sigma_{[i,j-1]} - i + 1)$, let $q = \min\{l\mid B_l\subseteq[i-1]\}$, and merge blocks according to the relation between $2r-q-1$ and $k$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: \sigma_{[j-1]} = \sigma_{[i-1]} \circ (\sigma_{[i,j-1]} - i + 1),\ q = \min\{l \mid B_l\subseteq [i-1]\},\ \psi(\sigma) = \begin{cases}\{B_1,\dots,B_{q-1},B_q\cup B_r,\dots,B_{r-1}\cup B_{2r-q-1},B_{2r-q},\dots,B_k\} & \text{if } 2r-q-1\le k\\ \{B_1,\dots,B_{q-1},B_q\cup B_r,\dots,B_{q+k-r}\cup B_k,B_{q+k-r+1},\dots,B_{r-1}\} & \text{otherwise}\end{cases}

paper_title: Two bijections on Tamari intervals
authors: Frédéric Chapoton, Grégory Chatel, Viviane Pons
source_object: An interval-poset $I$ (a labelled poset representing an interval of the Tamari lattice) with statistics $\Itrees(I)$ and $\Iir(I)$.
target_object: An interval-poset $J$ with $\Itrees(J) = \Iir(I)$ and $\Iir(J) = \Itrees(I)$.

algorithm_steps.description: Base case: if $I = \emptyset$, return $\beta(I) = \emptyset$.
Lower contacts decomposition: find the unique $k = \max\{i \mid \forall i' < i,\, i' \trprec i\}$; set $I_1 = \{i < k\}$, $I_2 = \{j > k\}$, and $r$ = number of children of $k$ in $\dec(I)$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $I = \mathrm{LC}(I_1, I_2, r)$ with $I_1 = \{i<k\}$, $I_2 = \{j>k\}$, $r = \#\{ \text{children of } k \text{ in } \dec(I)\}$

algorithm_steps.description: Recursively compute $\beta(I_1)$ and $\beta(I_2)$.

Initial rise composition: insert a new vertex into $J_2$. Let $k' = \Iir(J_2) - r + 1$. Insert a new vertex labelled $k'$ into $J_2$, shift the labels $\ge k'$ by 1, add increasing relation $k' \trprec k'+1$ (if $k'+1 \le |J_2|$), and adjust decreasing relations so that each former vertex keeps the same number of children in $\dec$.

Merge $J_1$ and $J_2'$: let $a = \Iir(J_1)$. Insert $J_2'$ right after $a$ (shift labels accordingly). Add decreasing relations $j \trprec a$ for all $j \in J_2'$. If $a \neq |J_1|$, add increasing relations $j \trprec b$ for all $j \in J_2'$, where $b = a + |J_2'| + 1$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\beta(I) = J = \mathrm{IR}(J_1, J_2, r)$, with $a = \Iir(J_1)$, $b = a + |J_2'| + 1$, and relations $\{j \trprec a \mid j \in J_2'\}$, $\{j \trprec b \mid j \in J_2'\}$ if $a \neq |J_1|$.

paper_title: Two bijections on Tamari intervals
authors: Frédéric Chapoton, Grégory Chatel, Viviane Pons
source_object: A closed flow $f$ on an ordered forest $F$: each node $v$ carries an input $i_v \ge -1$, the outgoing rate $r_v = i_v + \sum_{c \text{ child of } v} r_c$ satisfies $r_v \ge 0$, and the total exit rate $\sum_{v \text{ root}} r_v = 0$.
target_object: An interval-poset $I$ (representing a Tamari interval).

algorithm_steps.description: Label the nodes of $F$ recursively: start with the first root, then its children from left to right, then continue with the next root, etc. This gives a bijection between nodes and $\{1,\dots, n\}$.

Build the increasing relations of the interval-poset. For each vertex $i$, let $j$ be the first vertex with label greater than $i$ that is not a descendant of $i$ in $F$. Add $i \trprec j$ and, recursively, for all vertices on the rightmost branch of $i$, add the same relation to $j$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\forall i,\ \text{add } i' \trprec j \text{ for all } i' \text{ on the rightmost branch of } i,\ j = \min\{k > i \mid k \not\in \operatorname{Desc}(i)\}$

algorithm_steps.description: Process negative inputs in decreasing order of their labels. For a node $i$ with input $-1$, find its source $j$: the first (by label) descendant of $i$ with a strictly positive input. Add decreasing relations $j' \trprec i$ for all $i < j' \le j$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: For each $-1$ input at node $i$, let $j = \min\{ d \in \operatorname{Desc}(i) \mid i_d > 0 \}$ (in label order). Add $\{j' \trprec i \mid i < j' \le j\}$.

algorithm_steps.description: Repeat step 3 until no negative inputs remain. The final poset is the desired interval-poset.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $I = \text{Poset generated by increasing and decreasing relations}$

inverse_steps.description: Recover the forest $F$ from the increasing relations of $I$: the parent of $j$ is the largest $i < j$ with $i \not\trprec j$.

Reconstruct inputs: each vertex $i$ that has a decreasing relation $j \trprec i$ for some $j>i$ receives a $-1$ input; its source is the largest such $j$. Increase the input of that source accordingly.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $i_v = -1$ if $\exists j>i,\ j \trprec i$; then $\operatorname{source}(i) = \max\{ j>i \mid j \trprec i\}$
