inverse_steps.description: For a given historic tree \(H_n\), let \(H_k\) be the subtree induced by vertices with labels \(\leq k\).

If vertex \(k+1\) is attached to the \(i\)-th external vertex of \(H_k\), then in the corresponding history, \(T_{k+1}\) is obtained from \(T_k\) by inserting a key into the \(i\)-th leaf (and performing any necessary splits).

algorithm_steps.description: Given a parking-like structure $(\sp_i)_{i=1}^{n+1}$ with underlying sets $V_i$, define a total order $<_q$ on $U$ using the index of the block and the original order $<_U$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $u <_q u' \; \Longleftrightarrow \; \begin{cases} u <_U u' & \text{if } u,u'\in V_j \text{ for some } j, \\ j < k & \text{if } u\in V_j, u'\in V_k, j\neq k. \end{cases}$

algorithm_steps.description: Take $\sp_1$ as the root of the tree.
Order the elements of $U$ as $u_1 <_q u_2 <_q \cdots <_q u_n$. For $i=1,\dots,n$, attach $u_i$ to $\sp_{i+1}$, making $\sp_{i+1}$ the root of the subtree linked from $u_i$.

source_object: Dyck paths (lattice paths of upsteps $U=(1,1)$ and downsteps $D=(1,-1)$, same number of each, staying weakly above the horizontal line)
target_object: Dyck paths (same as source)

algorithm_steps.description: If the path is empty, return the empty path.
If the path is non-primitive with components $P_1,P_2,\dots,P_r$ ($r\ge 2$), apply $F$ to each component and concatenate.
If the path is primitive, write it as $P = U Q (UD)^i D$ where $i\ge 0$ and $Q$ is a Dyck path that is either empty or ends with $DD$.
If $Q$ is primitive, write $Q = U R D$ with $R$ a Dyck path, then set $F(P) = U^{i} F(R) U D^{i} D$.
If $Q$ is not primitive, then set $F(P) = U^{i+1} F(Q) D^{i+1}$.

inverse_steps.description: If the path is empty, return the empty path.
If the path is non-primitive with components $P_1,\dots,P_r$, apply $G$ to each and concatenate.
If the path is primitive, write it as $P = U^{i+1} Q D^{i+1}$ with $i\ge 0$ and $Q$ a non-primitive Dyck path ($Q=\varepsilon$ allowed).
If $Q$ ends with $UD$, write $Q = R U D$, then set $G(P) = U U G(R) D (UD)^{i} D$.
Otherwise, set $G(P) = U G(Q) (UD)^{i} D$.

source_object: descending plane partition of order $n$ with no special parts, having $p$ parts and $k$ parts equal to $n$

algorithm_steps.description: Construct a monotone triangle of order $n$ from the partition $\pi$ obtained in the pre-transformation. Start with bottom row $1,2,\ldots,n$. For $i$ from $n$ down to $1$, let $c_i$ be the number of parts equal to $i$ in $\pi$. Begin at the entry $i$ in the bottom row and form a path of $i$'s: at each step move northeast if possible, otherwise move northwest. Continue until exactly $c_i$ northwest steps have been taken. This fills the monotone triangle with entries.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: For $i=n,\dots,1$: start at $a_{n,i}$. At each step, if northeast step does not violate monotonicity, go northeast; else go northwest. Stop when $|\{ (r,c) : a_{r,c}=a_{r+1,c+1} \}| = c_i$.

algorithm_steps.description: The resulting array is a monotone triangle with no strict inequalities $a_{i,j} < a_{i-1,j} < a_{i,j+1}$. Convert it to an $n\times n$ permutation matrix using the standard bijection (record columns with partial sum 1 in each row).
algorithm_steps.math_formula: For row $i$, let $S_i$ be the set of columns where the prefix sum of 1's up to row $i$ is 1. Then $A_{i,j}=1$ if $j$ is the unique element in $S_i\setminus S_{i-1}$ (with $S_0=\emptyset$), and $0$ otherwise.

inverse_steps.description: Given an $n\times n$ permutation matrix $A$, convert it to its monotone triangle by recording the columns with partial sum 1 in each row.
inverse_steps.math_formula: For $i=1$ to $n$, let $S_i = \{ j \mid \sum_{k=1}^i A_{k,j} = 1 \}$. The $i$th row of the monotone triangle is the sorted elements of $S_i$.

inverse_steps.description: Extract all entries $a_{i,j}$ of the monotone triangle such that $a_{i,j}=a_{i+1,j+1}$. These entries form a partition $\pi$ with largest part at most $n$ and at most $i-1$ parts equal to $i$.

Use the map g (Notation 3.5) to insert single k's into u at positions dictated by ν_w, obtaining a word \underline{v} with no consecutive k's.

paper_title: A bijection for covered maps, or a shortcut between Harer-Zagier's and Jackson's formulas
source_object: covered maps $(M,S)$ where $M=(H,\sigma,\alpha)$ is a rooted map of genus $g$ with $n$ edges, and $S\subseteq H$ stable by $\alpha$ such that the submap $M_{|S}$ is a connecting unicellular map (i.e., spanning and unicellular)
target_object: pairs $(A,B)$ where $A$ is a rooted plane tree with $n$ edges and $B$ is a rooted bipartite unicellular map of genus $g$ with $n+1$ edges (white vertices correspond to vertices of $M$ and black vertices to faces of $M$)

algorithm_steps.description: Apply the orientation mapping $\Delta$ to $(M,S)$ to obtain a left-connected oriented map $(M,(I,O))$. Compute the motion function $\theta$ (the cyclic permutation of half-edges describing the tour of the submap $M_{|S}$) and define the ingoing half-edges $I$ accordingly.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\theta(h) = \sigma\alpha(h)$ if $h\in S$, $\theta(h)=\sigma(h)$ if $h\notin S$; $I = \{h\in S : \alpha(h)\lS h\} \cup \{h\notin S : h\lS \alpha(h)\}$, $O = H\setminus I$, where $\lS$ is the appearance order defined by $\theta$.

algorithm_steps.description: Apply the unfolding mapping $\Lambda$ to $(M,(I,O))$ to produce the plane tree $A$ and the mobile $B$. Introduce two new half-edges $i,o\notin H$, set $H'=H\cup\{i,o\}$, $I'=I\cup\{i\}$, $O'=O\cup\{o\}$, $\alpha'(i)=o$ and $\alpha'(h)=\alpha(h)$ for $h\in H$. Modify the vertex-permutation $\sigma'$ by inserting $i$ before the root $r$ and adding a fixed cycle $(o)$; similarly modify the face-permutation $\phi'$. Form the restrictions $\pi_\circ = \sigma'_{|I'}$, $\pi_\bu = \phi'_{|O'}$. Then define the tree $A$ with vertex-permutation $\tau$ on $H$ by $\tau' = \sigma' \pi_\circ^{-1}$, $\tau = \tau'_{|H}$, and root $t = \tau'(i)$. Define the mobile $B$ with vertex-permutation $\pi = \pi_\circ \pi_\bu^{-1}$ on $H'$ and root $i$.

inverse_steps.description: Given a pair $(A,B)$ of a plane tree and a coherently labelled bipartite unicellular map, form the oriented map $(M,(I,O))$ by the folding step $\Omega$. Start from the root-to-leaves orientation $(I,O)$ of $A$. Glue the first-corner of each vertex of $A$ to the corresponding white corner of $B$ (according to the clockwise order around $B$), then erase the edges and black vertices of $B$.
Apply the inverse orientation mapping $\Gamma$ to $(M,(I,O))$ to recover the covered map $(M,S)$ by following the motion function from the root and deciding membership in $S$ based on orientation.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $\theta = \begin{cases} \sigma\alpha(h) & h\in S \\ \sigma(h) & h\notin S \end{cases}$ and the procedure $\Gamma$ that reconstructs $S$.

paper_title: A new bijection relating $q$-Eulerian polynomials
source_object: $\mathfrak{S}_n$ (permutations $\sigma$ of $[n]$ with 2-descents and 2-inversions)
target_object: $\mathfrak{S}_n$ (permutations $\tau$ of $[n]$ with descents and exceedances)

algorithm_steps.description: Given $\sigma \in \mathfrak{S}_n$, determine $r = \des_2(\sigma)$, $s = \inv_2(\sigma)$, list $\DES_2(\sigma) = \{d_2^1 < \dots < d_2^r\}$ and $\INV_2(\sigma) = \{(i_1,j_1), \dots, (i_s,j_s)\}$.

For $k$ from $r$ down to $0$, using Algorithm~1 compute $c^0_k(\sigma)$ as the maximal length of sequences of 2-inversions starting from indices $\ge t_k(\sigma)$ and increasing in $\sigma(i)$-value, and set $I_{k-1}=I_k$ minus the involved pairs; then adjust $(c^0_k)$ to $(c_k)$ via Definition~7 (modifying when a dot descent is not in $\DES_2$).
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $c^0_k = \max \{ \sum_p n_p : (i_{k_p}) \in S_k \}$, $I_{k-1}=I_k \setminus \bigcup_{p} \{(i_{k_p^{\max}}^q, j_{k_p^{\max}}^q)\}$; $(c_k)$ obtained by shifting $+1/-1$ across gaps.

algorithm_steps.description: Construct an unlabelled planar graph $\mathcal{G}(\sigma)$ with $n$ vertices $v_1,\dots,v_n$: for each $k=0,\dots,r$, place $c_k$ circles on an ascending slope starting at abscissa $d_2^k+1$; the remaining $n-s$ vertices are dots, placed in ascending/descending slopes according to the word $\omega(\sigma) = \sigma(u_1)\cdots\sigma(u_{n-s})$ where $\{u_1<\cdots<u_{n-s}\} = [n] \setminus \{i_1,\dots,i_s\}$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\mathcal{G}(\sigma)$ has circle vertices at positions $d_2^k+1,\dots,d_2^k+c_k$ for $k=0,\dots,r$, dot vertices elsewhere; descent in dots matches descents in $\omega(\sigma)$.

algorithm_steps.description: Label the circles with the values $j_1,\dots,j_s$ using Algorithm~2: initially assign to each circle the set of $j$'s that can reach it; then, going from top to bottom in slopes, move the $a+b$ largest numbers downward and the smallest upward; resolve single-element sets.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: For circle at $v_i$, initial label $L_i = [i+1,n] \cap \{j_1,\dots,j_s\}$; when $v_i$ has $a$ circles above in descending slope and $b$ in ascending, remove the $a+b$ largest from $L_i$, and remove the $a+b$ smallest from those above; if $|L_i|=1$, set $\ell(v_i)=L_i$.

algorithm_steps.description: Label the dots with the remaining values $e_1<\dots<e_{n-s}$ using Algorithm~3: assign initial sets based on position and $u_k$; then adjust similarly as for circles; finally, for each $e_k$ in increasing order, pick the dot whose corresponding $\sigma(u)$ is smallest among those still containing $e_k$, assign $e_k$ to it, and remove from others.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $e_k = [n] \setminus \{j_1,\dots,j_s\}$; $v_{p_k}$ gets initial label $[\min(p_k,u_k)] \cap \{e_1,\dots,e_{n-s}\}$; after slope adjustment, for each $e_k$, $\ell(v_{p_{w^k_{i(k)}}}) = e_k$ where $i(k)$ gives minimal $\sigma(u_{w^k_{i}})$ among candidates.

algorithm_steps.description: The permutation $\varphi(\sigma)$ is the word $y_1 y_2 \dots y_n$ where $y_i$ is the label of $v_i$ in the completely labeled $\mathcal{G}(\sigma)$.

inverse_steps.description: Given $\tau \in \mathfrak{S}_n$, compute $s=\exc(\tau)$, $r$ and $\{d^{k,\tau}\}$ from $\DES(\tau)$; set $c_k^{\tau} = |\EXC(\tau) \cap (d^{k-1,\tau}, d^{k,\tau}]|$, $d_2^{k,\tau} = d^{k,\tau} - c_k^{\tau}$, and $t_k^{\tau}$ as in (22).
Build an empty linear graph $\mathcal{H}(\tau)$ with vertices $v_1,\dots,v_n$; box $v_{d_2^{k,\tau}}$ for each $k$; draw the end of an arc above $v_{\tau(i)}$ for $i\in\EXC(\tau)$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $\mathcal{H}(\tau)$: vertices $1,\dots,n$ in a row; boxes at $d_2^{k,\tau}$; arc-ends at $\tau(\EXC(\tau))$.

inverse_steps.description: Using Lemma~3, determine the start of each arc and add ascending/descending arrows between consecutive vertices where forced; define a partial order $\prec$ on vertices (Def.~8).
inverse_steps.math_formula: For each $j=\tau(l)$ with $l\in\EXC(\tau)$, arc starts from $i\in[t_{k}^{\tau},d^{k,\tau}]$ where $l\in]d_2^{k,\tau},d^{k,\tau}]$; arrows from known ascents/descents; $v_i \prec v_{i+1}$ if ascent, $v_i \succ v_j$ if arc.

inverse_steps.description: Label the vertices with $1,\dots,n$ using Algorithm~5, which at each step picks a minimal vertex with respect to $\prec$ (or uses a tie-breaking rule for dots based on $\tau$ values), assigns the next available integer, and completes arcs iteratively.
inverse_steps.math_formula: Initialize $S=[n]$, $l=1$. While $S\ne\emptyset$: find unique minimal $v_i$ on $S$ w.r.t. $\prec$, set $\ell(v_i)=l$, $l\leftarrow l+1$, $S\leftarrow S\setminus\{v_i\}$; if arc ends at $v_i$, label its start $v_j$ with $l$, update; if multiple minima, choose according to dot exchange property using $\tau$ values.

algorithm_steps.description: Label each vertex of the pointed bipartite quadrangulation $\mm$ by its distance to the basepoint $v_0$.

source_object: $J_n^{TL}$, the set of Temperley-Lieb diagrams (non-crossing pair partitions of $2n$ vertices on the lower half-plane) of degree $n$
target_object: $\YTL_n$, the set of Dyck paths from $(0,0)$ to $(2n,0)$ using steps $(1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$, non-collapsing and staying in $y\ge 0$

algorithm_steps.description: Generate a bracket sequence by scanning the vertices of the TL diagram from left to right.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: For $i=1,\dots,2n$, set $b_i = '('$ if vertex $i$ is the left endpoint of an arc, otherwise $b_i = ')'$.

algorithm_steps.description: Convert the bracket sequence into a step sequence for a Dyck path.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Define $s_i = 1$ if $b_i = '('$, and $s_i = 2$ if $b_i = ')'$; then $p = \TLinv(D) = (s_1,\dots,s_{2n})$ is the Dyck path corresponding to a walk with steps $(1,1)$ for $1$ and $(1,-1)$ for $2$.

inverse_steps.description: Apply the tiling map $\Psi|_{\YTL_n}$ to recover the TL diagram from the Dyck path.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $D = \Psi( \TLinv(D) )$, using tiling rules with two types of tiles (tile1 for step $1$, tileA for step $2$).

algorithm_steps.description: Determine the lower region of the overhang path and its root Dyck path.

algorithm_steps.description: Replace each tile in the root Dyck path with a patterned tile according to step type.

algorithm_steps.description: Replace tiles in the lower region above the root (skew diagram $p/r$) with crossing tiles.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: For each diamond tile in the region $p/r$, replace with tileX (contains two crossing arcs).

algorithm_steps.description: Tile the upper region (above the path) with half‑tiles and apply connecting rules to complete the diagram.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Fill the upper region with half‑tiles; use rules tile11, tile1L, tile1R, tile11top to connect vertical strands to the top horizontal line, producing the Brauer diagram $D = \Psi(p)$.

source_object: $J_n$, the set of Brauer diagrams of degree $n$
target_object: $\Y_n$, the set of overhang paths of degree $n$

algorithm_steps.description: Compute the projection $\Pi(D)$ onto a TL diagram via the right chain tree and geometric dual.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\Pi(D) = \gamma(\tau_R(D))$, where $\tau_R$ builds the right chain tree of $D$ and $\gamma$ takes the planar dual.

algorithm_steps.description: Convert the TL diagram $\Pi(D)$ into a Dyck path using the bracket encoding $\TLinv$.
For each secondary label $i$, determine the number $X_{D(i)}$ of steps by which the left endpoint of the arc must be moved rightward to achieve right‑agreement with $\Pi(D)$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: Inductively, let $D(0)=D$; for $j\ge 0$, if $D(j)$ and $\Pi(D)$ maximally right‑agree up to $x$, let $r$ be the number of fully agreeing arcs. The next arc has secondary label $r+1$; its left endpoint in $D(j)$ must be moved $X_{D(j)}$ steps to the right to agree with $\Pi(D)$. Set $D(j+1)=\delta D(j)$ and repeat until $\Pi(D)$ is reached.

algorithm_steps.description: Starting from the Dyck path $r$, for each $i$ append a left‑overhanging stack of $X_{D(i)}$ tiles after the step of form $(1,1)$ that carries label $i$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: At the $i$-th $(1,1)$-step of $r$ (according to left‑standard labelling), insert $X_{D(i)}$ repetitions of the pair $((-1,1),(1,1))$. The resulting path is $\Phi(D)$.

paper_title: A bijection between $321$- and $213$-avoiding permutations preserving $t$-stack-sortability
authors: Yang Li, Sergey Kitaev, Zhicong Lin, Jing Liu
source_object: $\S_n(321)$, the set of permutations of $[n]$ avoiding the pattern $321$
target_object: $\S_n(213)$, the set of permutations of $[n]$ avoiding the pattern $213$

algorithm_steps.description: Apply the Krattenthaler bijection $\rho$ to map a $321$-avoiding permutation to a Dyck path.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\rho(\pi)$ is the unique Dyck path from $(0,0)$ to $(n,n)$ that stays weakly above the diagonal and leaves all points $(i,\pi_i)$ strictly below it, chosen to be as close to the diagonal as possible.

algorithm_steps.description: Use the inverse of the classical bijection $\tau$ between plane trees and Dyck paths.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\tau^{-1}(D)$ is the plane tree with $n$ edges whose pre-order traversal, with east steps interpreted as down-edges and north steps as up-edges, yields $D$.

algorithm_steps.description: Apply the leftmost-child right-sibling bijection $\varphi$ from plane trees to binary trees.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\varphi(T)$ is the binary tree where for any non-root node $y$, $y$ is the left child of $x$ in $\varphi(T)$ iff $y$ is the leftmost child of $x$ in $T$, and $y$ is the right child of $x$ in $\varphi(T)$ iff $x$ is the closest left sibling of $y$ in $T$.

algorithm_steps.description: Apply the restricted mirror symmetry $\gamma$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\gamma(T)$ is obtained from $T$ by applying the mirror symmetry operation to every subtree whose root is a left child of a node on the right arm of $T$.

algorithm_steps.description: Label the binary tree by right pre-order and then apply $\lambda^{-1}$ (in-order reading) to obtain a $213$-avoiding permutation.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\lambda^{-1}(T)$ is the permutation obtained by in-order reading of $T$ after its nodes have been labeled with $[n]$ using right pre-order.

inverse_steps.description: Apply $\lambda$ to map the $213$-avoiding permutation to an increasing binary tree, then forget the labels to obtain a binary tree.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $\lambda(\sigma)$ is the increasing binary tree obtained by recursively building $T = (\text{left subtree}, \text{smallest element}, \text{right subtree})$; then $T'$ is the underlying binary tree.

inverse_steps.description: Apply $\gamma^{-1} = \gamma$ because $\gamma$ is an involution.
Apply $\varphi^{-1}$, the inverse of the leftmost-child right-sibling correspondence.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $\varphi^{-1}(T)$ is the plane tree where each node's children are its left child and all successive right children in $T$.

inverse_steps.description: Apply $\tau$, the classical bijection from plane trees to Dyck paths.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $\tau(T)$ is the Dyck path obtained by recording an east step for each down-edge and a north step for each up-edge during a pre-order traversal of $T$.

inverse_steps.description: Apply $\rho^{-1}$ to recover the $321$-avoiding permutation from the Dyck path.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $\rho^{-1}(D)$ is the unique $321$-avoiding permutation whose cross diagram $(i,\pi_i)$ lies immediately below the Dyck path $D$.

algorithm_steps.description: Apply full mirror symmetry $\beta$.

algorithm_steps.description: Apply the restricted mirror symmetry $\gamma$ (applies mirror symmetry only to subtrees rooted at left children of nodes on the right arm).

algorithm_steps.description: Convert back to a permutation via $\lambda^{-1}$ after labeling the tree by right pre-order.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\lambda^{-1}(V)$ is the permutation obtained by in-order reading of the tree $V$ after labeling its nodes with $[n]$ in right pre-order.

inverse_steps.description: Apply $\gamma^{-1} = \gamma$.
Apply $\beta^{-1} = \beta$.
Apply $\lambda^{-1}$ to recover the permutation.

paper_title: Bijective enumeration of rook walks
source_object: $[\ell-1]^k + \sum_{i=0, i\text{ odd}}^k \binom{[k]}{i} \times [\ell]^{k-i}$
target_object: $\sum_{i=0, i\text{ even}}^k \binom{[k]}{i} \times [\ell]^{k-i}$

algorithm_steps.description: If the input is an element $x \in [\ell-1]^k$, output the pair $(\emptyset, x)$, which corresponds to the $i=0$ (even) part of the target.

If the input is a pair $(S, y) \in \binom{[k]}{i} \times [\ell]^{k-i}$ with $i$ odd, first construct a sequence $x \in [\ell]^k$ by inserting $\ell$ at all positions in $S$ and filling the remaining positions with the entries of $y$ in order.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $x \in [\ell]^k$ such that $x_j = \ell$ for all $j \in S$, and $(x|_{[k] \setminus S}) = y$

algorithm_steps.description: Find the smallest index $m$ such that $x_m = \ell$. Since $y$ contains no $\ell$, this $m$ is guaranteed to be in $S$.
Remove $m$ from the set $S$ to obtain a new index set $S'$ of even size $i-1$.
Form the output sequence $y'$ by deleting from $x$ all positions that belong to $S'$ (these are exactly the $\ell$ entries).
Output the pair $(S', y')$, which belongs to $\binom{[k]}{i-1} \times [\ell]^{k-(i-1)}$ with even $i-1$.

inverse_steps.description: If the target element is $(S, x) \in \binom{[k]}{i} \times [\ell]^{k-i}$ with $i$ even and $x$ does not contain $\ell$ at any position not in $S$ (i.e., $x$ restricted to $[k]\setminus S$ has no $\ell$), then simply output $x$ as an element of $[\ell-1]^k$.

Otherwise, for a target element $(S, x)$ with $i$ even and $x$ containing at least one $\ell$ outside $S$, let $m$ be the smallest index with $x_m = \ell$. If $m \in S$, remove it ($S' = S \setminus \{m\}$, $i$ becomes odd); if $m \notin S$, add it ($S' = S \cup \{m\}$, $i$ becomes odd). Keep $x$ unchanged but now interpreted as an element of $[\ell]_{i'}^k$ with $i'$ odd. Finally, compress $x$ by removing all $\ell$ entries (which are exactly at the positions in $S'$) to obtain $y'$, and output $(S', y')$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $m = \min\{j \in [k] : x_j = \ell\}$; if $m \in S$, $S' = S \setminus \{m\}$ else $S' = S \cup \{m\}$; $y' = (x_j)_{j \in [k] \setminus S'}$; $f^{-1}(S, x) = (S', y')$

source_object: \mathscr{T}_n = \bigcup_{p=0}^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} \mathscr{T}_{n,p}, where \mathscr{T}_{n,p} is the set of colored complete ternary trees with p internal vertices, each vertex v assigned a nonnegative integer color c_v such that \sum_v c_v = n-2p.
target_object: \mathscr{B}_n, the set of complete binary trees with n internal vertices.

algorithm_steps.description: For each vertex v of T with color number c_v=k, remove the color and attach a right path P=v_1\cdots v_k of length k to v such that v is the right child of v_k and v_1 is a child of the father of v (if exists), then annex a left leaf to each v_i (i=1..k).
algorithm_steps.math_formula: T \mapsto T' where for every vertex v with c_v=k, v is replaced by a path (v_1,\dots,v_k) such that child_father(v_1) = original_father_v_child, right_child(v_k)=v, and for i=1..k, left_child(v_i) = new leaf.

algorithm_steps.description: For each internal vertex v of T^* (obtained from T) with out-degree 3, let its three subtrees be T_1,T_2,T_3. Remove T_1 and T_2, attach a left child v' to v, and make T_1,T_2 the left and right subtrees of v' respectively.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: v(T_1,T_2,T_3) \mapsto v(v'(T_1,T_2),T_3), where v' is a new internal vertex.

inverse_steps.description: In B, choose any maximal L-path P=v_1\cdots v_k (k\ge 3). For i=1,\dots,\lfloor (k-1)/2 \rfloor, let v_{2i-1} absorb its left child v_{2i} (i.e., merge the left child into v_{2i-1} so that v_{2i-1} becomes a ternary internal vertex).
inverse_steps.math_formula: For a maximal L-path v_1\cdots v_k, transform (v_1(v_2,\dots)) \mapsto \tilde{v}_1 with ternary children (left, middle, right) taken from the structure.

inverse_steps.description: In the tree T' obtained from B, choose any maximal R-path Q=u_1\cdots u_k, let u be the right child of u_k. Then u absorbs all vertices u_1,\dots,u_k and receives color number c_u = k.
inverse_steps.math_formula: Q \mapsto u with c_u = k, where u is the right child of u_k and the subtrees of u_1,\dots,u_k become subtrees of u (restructured).

paper_title: A bijection between 2-triangulations and pairs of non-crossing Dyck paths
source_object: A $2$-triangulation of a convex $n$-gon, represented as a set of $2n-10$ crosses in the board $\Lambda_n = \{ (a,b) \mid 1 \le a < b-2 \le n-2,\ a > b-n+2 \}$ (trivial diagonals omitted).
target_object: A pair $(P,Q)$ of Dyck paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n-4,n-4)$ such that $P$ never goes below $Q$.

algorithm_steps.description: Initialize the board $\Lambda_n$ with the given crosses. Index columns $4,\dots,n$ and rows $1,\dots,n-3$. Create $n-3$ blocks, where block $j$ initially contains only column $j+3$ ($j=1,\dots,n-3$).

algorithm_steps.description: Repeat steps 2–5 exactly $n-5$ times. After all iterations, all $2n-10$ crosses are colored, and only two blocks remain.

paper_title: A bijection between two subfamilies of Motzkin paths
authors: Nancy S. S. Gu, Helmut Prodinger
source_object: Motzkin paths with $n$ up steps $u$, $n$ down steps $d$, $n$ horizontal steps $h$, decomposable as $A_0 D_1 A_1 D_2 \ldots A_{t-1} D_t$ where each $A_i$ consists only of $h$ and $u$, each $D_i$ is a nonempty block of consecutive $d$ steps, and the numbers $d_i=|D_i|$, $u_i = \# \text{ of } u \text{ in } A_i$ satisfy $\sum_{k=1}^i d_k \le \sum_{k=0}^{i-1} u_k$ for $1\le i\le t-1$ and $\sum_{k=1}^t d_k = \sum_{k=0}^{t-1} u_k$.
target_object: S-Motzkin paths: Motzkin paths with $n$ up steps $u$, $n$ down steps $d$, $n$ horizontal steps $h$, such that deleting all down steps leaves the alternating sequence $huhu\dots hu$ (starting with $h$, ending with $u$).

algorithm_steps.description: Decompose the given AM-type Motzkin path into blocks $A_0, D_1, A_1, D_2, \dots, A_{t-1}, D_t$ where each $A_i$ contains only $h$ and $u$, each $D_i$ is a block of consecutive $d$, and all blocks are nonempty. Record $d_i = |D_i|$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $P = A_0 D_1 A_1 D_2 \dots A_{t-1} D_t$, $d_i \leftarrow |D_i|$.

algorithm_steps.description: Transform each $A_i$ into a Dyck path $\overline{A_i}$ by replacing every $h$ with $u$ and every $u$ with $d$.

From each Dyck path $\overline{A_i}$, build an S-Motzkin subpath $A_i'$ by inserting horizontal steps $h$ in the first possible positions when scanning left to right: each $h$ is placed so that it is the first horizontal step on its height and there are no two $h$ on the same height with all intermediate steps above that height.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $A_i' \leftarrow \operatorname{insert\_h}(\overline{A_i})$ where the insertion rule guarantees that $A_i'$ is an S-Motzkin path.

algorithm_steps.description: Initialize the output path as $A_0'$, and let $u_0$ be the number of $u$ steps in $A_0'$.

For $i=1$ to $t-1$, insert $A_i'$ into the current path using $d_i$ as a pointer: locate the $d_i$-th up step counting from the start of $A_{i-1}'$ (if $d_i \le u_{i-1}$, this step lies in $A_{i-1}'$ and is not the last up step of $A_{i-1}'$ unless $d_i=u_{i-1}$; if $d_i > u_{i-1}$, search further left among earlier $A_j'$). Insert $A_i'$ immediately after that up step, except when the located step is the last up step of some $A_s'$; then place $A_i'$ at the end of $A_s'$. Update $u_i \leftarrow \#\{u \in A_i'\}$.
algorithm_steps.math_formula: $\text{current\_path} \leftarrow \text{insert } A_i' \text{ after the } d_i\text{-th } u \text{ counted from the beginning of } A_{i-1}' \text{ (with the described exceptions)}$.

algorithm_steps.description: The final current path is the desired S-Motzkin path.

inverse_steps.description: Scan the S-Motzkin path from left to right to identify paired horizontal steps $h_0, h_1, \dots, h_{t-1}$: the first $h$ is always paired; for each paired $h_i$, if there is a next $h$ on the same height and all steps between them are never below this height, that $h$ is also paired. The subpath between a paired $h_i$ and the end of the corresponding block forms a building stone $A_i'$. Record the distances $d_i$ as the number of up steps encountered from the start of $A_{i-1}'$ to the $u$ just before $h_i$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: Let $h_0, h_1, \dots, h_{t-1}$ be the paired horizontal steps; $A_i'$ is the subpath starting at $h_i$ and ending where the next paired block begins; $d_i$ is the count of up steps from the beginning of $A_{i-1}'$ to the $u$ immediately preceding $h_i$.

inverse_steps.description: Delete all horizontal steps from each $A_i'$, then change every $u$ to $h$ and every $d$ to $u$ to obtain $A_i$.
inverse_steps.math_formula: $A_i \leftarrow \text{delete all } h \text{ from } A_i' \text{ and apply } (u \to h,\; d \to u)$.

inverse_steps.description: Construct the AM-type Motzkin path as $A_0 D_1 A_1 D_2 \dots D_{t-1} A_{t-1}$, where $D_i$ is a block of $d_i$ consecutive $d$ steps. Append additional $d$ steps at the end to make the total number of $d$ steps equal $n$ (automatic by the conditions).
inverse_steps.math_formula: $\Psi(P) = A_0 D_1 A_1 D_2 \dots D_{t-1} A_{t-1}$, with $|D_i| = d_i$ and final block of $d$ steps added to match the required count.
